title: 第六章　他们建设了社会主义，1929—1935

children: 我们正全速沿着工业化之路奔向社会主义，把俄国由来已久的落后状态抛在身后。我们正在成为一个金属国家、一个汽车国家、一个拖拉机国家。当我们让苏联坐上汽车、让庄稼汉开上拖拉机时，就让那些以“文明”自鸣得意的可敬资本家来追赶我们吧。到那时我们再看，哪些国家可以被“归类”为落后，哪些为先进。

We are going full steam ahead along the road of industrialization to socialism, leaving behind our century-old Russian backwardness. We are becoming a metallic country, an automotive country, a tractor country. When we have put the USSR in an automobile, and the muzhik on a tractor, then let the esteemed capitalists, preening themselves with their “civilization,” try to overtake us. We will see then which countries can be “classified” as backward and which as advanced.
不，同志们……我们绝不能降低［工业化的］速度。
No, comrades,… we must not lower the tempo [of industrialization].

……降低速度就意味着落后；而落后就要挨打……旧俄国的历史表明，她因落后而不断挨打。她被蒙古汗打过，被土耳其贝伊打过，被瑞典封建主打过，被波兰—立陶宛老爷打过，被英法资本家打过，被日本男爵打过，被所有人打过——因为她的落后。因为军事落后，因为文化落后，因为政治落后，因为工业落后，因为农业落后。她挨打，是因为打她有利可图，而且不受惩罚。你们记得革命前那位诗人［涅克拉索夫］的话：“你又贫穷，你又富饶，你又强大，你又无力。俄罗斯母亲。”

…To reduce the tempo would mean to fall behind; and those who fall behind are beaten…. The history of old Russia showed her constantly beaten for her backwardness. She was beaten by the Mongol Khans, she was beaten by the Turkish Beys, she was beaten by the Swedish feudal lords, she was beaten by Polish-Lithuanian Pans, she was beaten by Anglo-French capitalists, she was beaten by Japanese barons, she was beaten by all—for her backwardness. For military backwardness, for cultural backwardness, for political backwardness, for industrial backwardness, for agricultural backwardness. She was beaten because to beat her was profitable and went unpunished. You remember the words of the pre-revolutionary poet [Nekrasov]: “Thou art poor and thou art plentiful, thou art mighty and thou art helpless. Mother Russia.”
……这就是为什么列宁在十月说：“要么灭亡，要么赶上并超过先进资本主义国家。”
…This is why Lenin said in October: “The choice is either death or catching up with and overtaking the advanced capitalist countries.”
……我们比先进国家落后五十年或一百年。我们必须在十年内跑完这段距离。要么我们做到，要么他们把我们碾碎。
…We are fifty or a hundred years behind the advanced countries. We must run that same distance in ten years. Either we do it or they crush us.

zh: 斯大林三十年代五年计划所建设的社会主义，是苏联实验的顶点。它把1917年后布尔什维克多年探索推向高潮，并创造了延续到1991年苏联解体的基本制度。列宁战时共产主义所提供的未来秩序草图，如今被这位钢铁之人通过一场新攻势彻底充实。1929年，关于总路线的辩论永远结束：布尔什维克不再谈论他们打算做什么，而是终于动手做了。
en: The socialism built by Stalin’s Five-Year Plans of the 1930s was the climax of the Soviet experiment. It brought to a culmination all the years of Bolshevik searching after 1917, and it created the basic institutions of the Soviet system as it would exist until the collapse of 1991. The rough sketch of the future order offered by Lenin’s War Communism was now completely filled in through a new Offensive by the man of steel. In 1929, debate on the General Line ended for good: The Bolsheviks stopped talking about what they were going to do and at last did it.

zh: 斯大林问题
en: THE STALIN QUESTION

zh: 斯大林在这个决定性十年的统治，被称为第二次俄国革命，这个名称相当贴切。它也被称为“帖木儿式的社会主义原始积累”，
这甚至更贴切。然而两个标签都没有真正传达事件的特殊性：三十年代俄国的转变在规模上前所未有，其使用的手段也同样独特，混合着疯狂与犯罪，同时——必须承认——也有宏大和史诗性。
en: Stalin’s rule during this decisive decade has been called the Second Russian Revolution, and the designation is quite apt. It has also been called “primitive socialist accumulation by the methods of Tamerlane,”

and this is even more apt. Yet neither label really conveys the specificity of the event: The transformation of Russia during the thirties was unprecedented in scope, to the same degree as the means employed to achieve it were unique in their mixture of the insane and the criminal with—it must be admitted—the grandiose and the epic.

zh: 这提出了另一个重大历史解释问题。
上一章论证，选择强制道路通向社会主义并非偶然，而是一个布尔什维克党在生存危机中的逻辑路线。但这并不自动意味着，斯大林实施这一选择时那种异常残暴的方式，同样受党的精神气质支配。集体化和工业化被强加的速度，不是一个自动进程的结果，而是有意识决定的结果。而1929年后，斯大林的权力如此之大，以至于最关键的决定由他亲自作出，或至少由他监督。
en: This poses another major problem of historical interpretation.

The previous chapter argued that the choice of a coercive road to socialism was no accident but the logical course for a Bolshevik Party in a crisis of survival. Yet it does not automatically follow that the extraordinarily brutal manner in which Stalin implemented that choice was equally governed by the Party’s ethos. The pace at which collectivization and industrialization were forced was not the outcome of an automatic process but the result of conscious decisions. And after 1929 Stalin’s power was so great that he personally made, or at least supervised, the most crucial of those decisions.

zh: 因此，制度逻辑与斯大林个人角色的问题并不随着大转折结束，而是贯穿整个三十年代，从集体化到清洗。集体化的罪行有多少应归于斯大林个人的犯罪性格？清洗的疯狂有多少应归于他本人可能的精神失常？这种探究会说：列宁和托洛茨基（两人都是强硬的布尔什维克，完全可能在1929年采取强制政策）肯定不会故意饿死农民或谋杀革命同志。斯大林本人的偏执和虐待狂倾向，必定是决定因素，使他的统治在布哈林的比喻中像成吉思汗的回归。
en: So the question of the logic of the system versus Stalin’s personal role does not end with the Great Break but continues throughout the thirties, from the collectivization to the Purges. How much of the criminality of the collectivization was due to Stalin’s own criminal character? How much of the madness of the Purge was due to his own possible insanity? Surely—this line of inquiry goes—neither Lenin nor Trotsky (both hard Bolsheviks who could quite conceivably have adopted a coercive policy in 1929) would have deliberately starved the peasants or murdered revolutionary comrades. The personal paranoia and the individual sadism of Stalin the man must constitute the decisive element that made his reign seem, in Bukharin’s metaphor, like the return of Genghis Khan.

zh: 这种论证常常还加上一个主题：斯大林的第二次革命（不同于1917年的第一次革命）是一场自上而下的革命，而自上而下的革命是俄国追赶先进西方的悠久方法。

于是斯大林主义代表了对俄国专制更极端阶段的回归，如伊凡雷帝或彼得大帝时期。粗看之下，这种解释似乎非常可信。的确，斯大林本人喜欢把他粗暴的国家建设与这两位沙皇相比，彼得代表计划，伊凡代表恐怖。然而，明智的做法是在考察斯大林本人的施政记录之前保留判断，并且首先不是到遥远的世纪，而是到产生这场自上而下革命的实际环境中去寻找斯大林主义的根源。在这条探究线索中，斯大林的人格远比过去专制君主的幽灵更切合问题。
en: To this argumentation is often added the theme that Stalin’s Second Revolution (unlike the first Revolution of 1917) was a revolution from above, and revolution from above is the time-honored Russian method of catching up with the advanced West.

Thus Stalinism represented a reversion to the more extreme phases of Russian autocracy, as under Ivan the Terrible or Peter the Great. And at a superficial glance this explanation seems eminently plausible. Indeed, Stalin himself liked to compare his rough nation-building with that of these two tsars, Peter for the Plan and Ivan for the Terror. Yet it would be prudent to reserve judgement on this matter until Stalin’s own record has been examined, and to seek the sources of Stalinism, in the first instance, not in remote centuries but in the actual circumstances that produced the revolution from above. Here, in this line of inquiry, Stalin’s personality is far more germane than are the ghosts of autocrats past.

zh: 即便如此，在这一点上也应当谨慎，因为斯大林阴郁的形象，如同希特勒同样阴森的形象，很容易遮蔽他的时代和他所代表的制度。于是，日常用语中的“斯大林主义”往往意味着一种统治风格——一种极端的个人暴政、一种例外的专制、或一种超级独裁——由斯大林这个人创造并维持。但这些希腊罗马术语，如同成吉思汗的典故一样，都不足以说明斯大林现象的历史特殊性。
en: Even so, caution is in order on this score, too, for Stalin’s lugubrious figure, like Hitler’s equally macabre one, can easily overshadow his period and the system he represented. Thus “Stalinism” in common parlance too often means a style of rule—an extreme personal tyranny, an exceptional despotism, or a superdictatorship—created and sustained by the man, Stalin. But these Greek and Roman terms do not do justice, any more than does the invocation of Genghis Khan, to the historical particularity of the Stalin phenomenon.

zh: 因此，斯大林主义也必须被视为一个依靠高度官僚化和恐怖手段进行控制的
。然而即便这样做，这个制度的起源仍常常不是用结构性因素解释，而是用暴君过度的野心解释。其后果是：一旦“主义”的邪恶作者消失，制度本身就可以被认为已经终结。于是，如我们所见，在西方和苏联的用法中，斯大林主义有时被说成与布尔什维主义和列宁主义完全不同的现象。
用苏联的话说，这种评估被表述为“个人崇拜”，意思是本来健全的社会主义被一位领袖不当的、偶然的权力所“扭曲”。于是，落后状态的逻辑、铁板一块的党的逻辑、社会主义原始积累的逻辑、意识形态统治的党治的逻辑，都被一种抽象暴政即“崇拜”的逻辑遮蔽了。
en: So Stalinism must also be viewed as a

of hyperbureaucratic and terroristic control. Yet even when this is done, the system’s genesis is still too often explained not by structural factors but by the tyrant’s overweening ambition. The consequence of this is that once the evil author of the “ism” has disappeared, the system itself may be considered to have ended. Thus in both Western and Soviet usage, as we have seen, Stalinism was at times held to be a completely different phenomenon from Bolshevism and Leninism.

In Soviet parlance this assessment was expressed as “the cult of personality,” which meant that an otherwise sound socialism was “distorted” by the undue and accidental power of one leader. So the logics of backwardness, of the monolithic Party, of primitive socialist accumulation, and of the ideocratic partocracy were all obscured by a logic of abstract tyranny, the “cult.”

zh: 这种方法可以称为历史的“坏人”理论。它的吸引力在于把痛苦的过去人格化，集中到一个单一的恶的焦点上，从而简化它。但正如刚才指出的，这种普遍倾向的缺陷在于，它遮蔽了个人背后更深层的制度，或至少使制度从属于他的持续在场。于是，他之前的东西和他之后的东西可以被视为不同的制度，并产生一种信念：一旦恶的焦点消失，这个制度就能恢复健康的常态。因此，对斯大林主义的“坏人”解释与偏离论相关。的确，斯大林的邪恶人格是“偏离”论的核心，因为除此之外没有别的办法解释一个本来健康的有机体如何出了毛病。斯大林爬上独裁地位，是因为如布哈林喜欢说的，他是一个“无原则的阴谋家，把一切都服从于保全自身权力的目的”。
en: This approach might be called the “bad man” theory of history. Its appeal is to simplify a painful past by personalizing it and concentrating it in a single focus of evil. ^180^But, as just noted, the defect of this universal penchant is that it obscures the deeper system behind the man, or at least subordinates it to his continuing presence, Thus, what came before him and what came after can be viewed as a different system, and the belief arises that once the focus of evil has disappeared this system can recover a healthy normality. Hence, the “bad man” approach to Stalinism is related to the aberration thesis. Indeed, Stalin’s evil personality is at the heart of the “aberration” thesis because there is no alternative way to explain how an otherwise healthy organism went awry. Stalin climbed to dictatorship because he was, as Bukharin liked to see it, “an unprincipled intriguer who subordinates everything to the preservation of his own power.”

zh: 斯大林确实是个坏人，而且是个非常坏的人，随着年龄增长越来越坏。但要解释他二十五年统治中的重大政策，还需要更多东西。他必须有一个制度和观念的语境，在其中工作，并通过它宣泄困扰其心灵的任何黑暗驱动力。此外，我们必须假设，俄国和党内还有相当多其他人，同样有严酷的童年和残忍的父亲，同样神经质、渴望权力，却没有成为重要的政治人物。除非先有一个需要解决的政治问题，心理学不会转化为政治。在解释任何政治领袖的政策时，我们必须像他行动时那样，接受政治动机的优先性。那些仅仅利用权力宣泄自身精神病态的政治领袖，掌权时间不会很长，彼得三世、保罗一世，乃至更早的康茂德皇帝的例子都说明了这一点。但斯大林持续了四分之一个世纪，按照任何世俗的判断标准，都必须被视为世界历史性的成功：毕竟，他建设了社会主义，打败了法西斯主义，创造了一个苏维埃帝国。历史中的心理学还原论，并不比社会经济还原论更有效。因此，本章的目的之一，是从苏维埃制度推导斯大林的政策，而不是反过来处理二者的关系。
en: Now, Stalin was a bad man, indeed a very bad man, and he grew steadily worse with age. But much more than this is needed to explain the momentous policies of his twenty-five-year reign. He had to have a context of institutions and ideas within which to work and through which to vent whatever dark drives haunted his psyche. Moreover, we must assume that there were quite a number of other individuals in Russia and in the Party who had equally harsh childhoods and cruel fathers, who were equally neurotic and thirsty for power, but who did not become politically significant figures. Psychology does not translate into politics unless there is first a political problem to be met. In explaining any political leader’s policies we must accept, just as he does when he acts, the primacy of political motivation. Political leaders who use their power simply to act out their psychoses do not keep power very long, as the cases of Peter III, or Paul I, and on back to Emperor Commodus, serve to illustrate. But Stalin lasted a quarter of a century, and by any mundane standards of judgement he must be considered a world-historical success: After all, he built socialism, defeated fascism, and created a Soviet empire. Psychological reductionism in history works no better than socioeconomic reductionism. One of the purposes of this chapter, therefore, is to derive Stalin’s policies from the Soviet system rather than to work the relationship the other way around.

zh: 历史的个人化并不只限于负面现象。还有一种“好人”史观，其突出例子是西方对戈尔巴乔夫的崇拜；这种崇拜有六年之久维持了一种幻觉，以为共产主义正在自我改革，而实际上它正在崩溃。的确，公共生活的个人化几乎无处不在——从罗慕路斯到乔治·华盛顿——因为它似乎使现实对每个人都变得容易理解。
en: ^180^The personalization of history is not confined to negative phenomena. There is also a “good man” view of history, of which a striking example was the Western cult of Gorbachev, which for six years sustained the illusion that Communism was reforming itself when in fact it was collapsing. Indeed, personalization of public life is well-nigh universal—from Romulus to George Washington—because it seems to make reality easily comprehensible to everybody.

zh: 不过，在共产主义的政治语境中，斯大林的个人传记是相关的，最基本的事实如下：他是列宁政治局中唯一来自“人民”的成员。父亲是酗酒的乡村鞋匠，后来成了鞋厂工人；母亲是不识字的虔诚农民。他在东正教神学院未完成的教育，给了他成为熟读俄国文学而不熟悉欧洲文学的自学者的装备。但他没有成为
，因为与真正的知识分子不同，他对观念本身不感兴趣，更不关心其道德含义。尽管如此，一旦成为布尔什维克，他确实接受了马克思主义意识形态的系统的基础训练。没有理由怀疑他对马克思主义承诺的真诚，无论他运用得多么粗糙：这为他整个成年生活提供了世界观的基础。在举止上，他始终保持粗鲁和平民气，但他并不是许多俄国人所认为的那种社会类型——在他的母语格鲁吉亚语中称为
，俄语中称为
（大致是“街头恶棍”或“街头幸存者”），那种在适当环境下容易转向犯罪的人。
en: Still, within the political context of Communism, Stalin’s personal biography is pertinent, and the most basic facts are these: He was the only member of Lenin’s Politburo who came from “the people.” His father was an alcoholic village cobbler who became a worker in a shoe factory, and his mother was an illiterate, pious peasant. His uncompleted education in a seminary of the Orthodox Church gave him the equipment to become a well-read autodidact in Russian, though not in European, literature. He did not become an

, however, because, unlike real members of the intelligentsia, he was not interested in ideas as such, and still less in their moral implications. Nonetheless, once he became a Bolshevik he did receive a thorough grounding in Marxist ideology. There is no reason to doubt the genuineness of his commitment to Marxism, however crudely he applied it: It furnished the basis of his worldview for the whole of his adult life. In manner he always remained rough and plebeian, but he was not, as many Russians believe, a social type that in his native Georgian is called
and in Russian
(approximately “street tough” or “street survivor”), a type that would easily turn to crime in appropriate circumstances.

zh: 相反，他成了一个意志坚强的革命者，并以此身份为其反社会能量找到了“合法”出口。但许多其他布尔什维克也是如此；社会革命党战斗组织即恐怖主义一翼的成员也是如此，其中许多人后来进了契卡。（总体而言，孟什维克往往更知识分子化，也更不习惯于暴力。）斯大林早年在高加索，也留下了把罢工和示威变成肢体冲突的记录。但像他这种脾气的人成为共产党首脑，并不是简单的坏运气：党通过密谋式的招募、组织结构和战斗精神，把许多这样的人带到掌权的位置。的确，在他自上而下的革命期间，他们就在斯大林周围；没有这些志同道合的人，这场革命根本不可能。
en: Instead he became a tough-minded revolutionary, and in that capacity he acquired a “legitimate” outlet for his asocial energies. But this can be said of many other Bolsheviks; it is also true of members of the Combat Organization, or terrorist wing, of the Socialist Revolutionaries, many of whom later wound up in the Cheka. (The Mensheviks, by and large, tended to be more intellectual and less comfortable with violence.) And Stalin in his early days in the Caucasus compiled a record of turning strikes and demonstrations into physical brawls. But it was no simple stroke of bad luck that someone of his temper became head of the Communist Party: By its conspiratorial recruitment, structure, and militant ethos, the Party brought many such people to positions of authority. Indeed, they were all around Stalin during his revolution from above; without such kindred spirits this revolution would not have been possible at all.

zh: 斯大林的政治生涯完全归功于列宁。1912年，列宁需要一位少数民族出身的人来表达他关于民族主义革命潜力的新观点，斯大林被选中做这件事。更重要的是，同一年列宁把他吸纳进党中央委员会（同时把另一个边缘人物、警察密探罗曼·马利诺夫斯基也安进该机构）。因此，1917年3月斯大林从西伯利亚流放地回到彼得格勒时，是当地主要的布尔什维克；而且从那时起，他一直留在党的最高领导层。
en: Stalin owed his political career entirely to Lenin. In 1912 Lenin needed someone from a minority nationality to express his own new views on the revolutionary potential of nationalism, and Stalin was tapped for the job. Even more important, in the same year Lenin coopted him into the Party’s Central Committee (at the same time that he put another marginal type, the police agent Roman Malinovskii, on that body). Thus, when Stalin returned to Petrograd from Siberian exile in March 1917, he was the chief Bolshevik in town; moreover, from that time on he remained in the top leadership of the Party.

zh: 然而起初，斯大林的角色是列宁忠实的副手。事实上，他是唯一没有与列宁发生重大公开分歧的重要布尔什维克：托洛茨基、布哈林、季诺维也夫以及中央委员会大多数其他成员，从十月到布列斯特-立托夫斯克及以后，都曾在某个重大问题上与这位“老头子”冲突。然而在整个1917年，对公众来说斯大林只是一个“灰色模糊的影子”，用当时一位孟什维克编年史家的话说；他在十月没有可见的角色，这是他革命记录中一个刺眼的空白，后来多年一直压在他心头，直到掌权后他改写记录，把自己写成列宁在十月革命的共同缔造者，从而篡夺了托洛茨基的位置。
en: At the beginning, however, Stalin’s role was to be Lenin’s faithful second. Indeed, he was the only important Bolshevik not to have a major public disagreement with Lenin: Trotsky, Bukharin, Zinoviev, and most other members of the Central Committee had clashed with the “Old Man” on one or another major issue, from October to BrestLitovsk and beyond. Yet to the public throughout 1917 Stalin was only a “gray blur,” to use the expression of a Menshevik chronicler of that year, and he played no visible role in October, a glaring gap in his revolutionary record that weighed on him in later years until, once in power, he rewrote the record to make himself coauthor with Lenin of October, thus usurping Trotsky’s place.

zh: 但在真实历史中，斯大林只是在内战期间才真正崭露头角；当时他担任民族人民委员，尤其是各条战线的政治委员，特别是1918年至关重要的察里津（后改名斯大林格勒）战役，以及1920年的波兰战争。正是在这一时期，他获得了一个由亲信和盟友组成的网络，其中大多是同僚政委；这些人成为他在党内的特别扈从，1929年后又构成他在建设社会主义的新内战中的最高指挥班子：再次列举，莫洛托夫、卡冈诺维奇、伏罗希洛夫、米高扬、基洛夫、日丹诺夫、安德烈耶夫、奥尔忠尼启则和古比雪夫。在集结这批追随者时，他并没有违反当时的党规；所有其他布尔什维克领袖都有自己的追随者，这些人后来形成了二十年代的反对派。然而尽管地位上升，斯大林仍小心地至少在公开场合表现得是列宁在行政事务上忠实的首席副手；如前所述，这也是他1922年被任命为总书记的原因之一。然而即便那时，他的同事也没有把他视为重要人物，更不视为威胁；在托洛茨基看来，他只是一个“庸才”。
en: In real history, however, Stalin came into his own only during the Civil War, when he served as People’s Commissar for Nationalities and, above all, as a political commissar on various fronts, especially in the vital battle for Tsaritsyn (later renamed Stalingrad) in 1918, and then in the Polish War of 1920. It is in this period that he acquired a network of cronies and allies, mostly fellow commissars, who would be his special retainers within the Party and who, after 1929, would furnish his high command in the new civil war to build socialism: Molotov, Kaganovich, Voroshilov, Mikoyan, Kirov, Zhdanov, Andreev, Ordzhonikidze, and Kuibyshev, to name them once again. In assembling this clientele he was not violating the Party norms of the time; all the other Bolshevik leaders had their clients, who later formed the oppositions of the twenties. Despite this increased status, however, Stalin was still careful to appear, at least publicly, as Lenin’s faithful chief lieutenant for administrative matters, and, as already noted, this is one reason why he was made General Secretary in 1922. Even then, however, he was not perceived by his colleagues as an important figure, still less as a threat; to Trotsky he appeared only as a “mediocrity.”

zh: 垂危的列宁是最先对斯大林担任“总书记”新角色表示怀疑的人之一。1922年，两人在新苏联的形式上发生冲突：斯大林当时正以集中化精神起草其宪法，而列宁想要一个较为松散的结构。这场冲突导致列宁的政治“遗嘱”，通常被解读为斯大林篡夺了老头子的“长袍”，因而斯大林主义不是真正的布尔什维主义。然而这些口授笔记绝非如此简单。列宁只认真考虑过两位副手托洛茨基和斯大林作为可能的继承人：他称他们为“党内最有能力的领袖”，并把大部分评论用于讨论他们的性格。季诺维也夫和加米涅夫加在一起只用一句话打发，布哈林得到的评价略多，而当时并不显眼的皮亚塔科夫似乎只是为了给人一种真正全面考察的印象才被列入。然而，在单独点出斯大林和托洛茨基之后，列宁随即对两人都作了尖锐批评。斯大林被批评“太粗鲁”，作为总书记积累了“过大的权力”。因此列宁提议把他从那个职位上撤下，但并非逐出最高领导层，因为列宁并不打算像有时被指控的那样在政治上消灭斯大林。然后列宁不偏不倚地批评托洛茨基过分倾向于“行政方面”，用大白话说就是他太专横。更负面的评论针对季诺维也夫和加米涅夫，他们在十月的表现被称为“绝非偶然”，也针对布哈林，他被称作“蹩脚的马克思主义者”。
en: The dying Lenin was among the first to express doubts about Stalin in his new role as “Gensek.” In 1922 the two men clashed over the form of the new Soviet Union, whose constitution Stalin was then writing in a centralizing spirit while Lenin wanted a somewhat looser structure. This clash led to Lenin’s political “testament,” which has usually been read as proof that Stalin usurped the Old Man’s “caftan” and, therefore, that Stalinism was not true Bolshevism. These dictated notes, however, are by no means so simple. Lenin took only two of his lieutenants, Trotsky and Stalin, seriously as possible successors: He rated them the “ablest leaders of the Party” and devoted the bulk of his remarks to a discussion of their characters. Zinoviev and Kamenev together were dismissed in one line, while Bukharin rated barely more, and Piatakov, hardly prominent at the time, seemed to have been thrown in only to give the impression of a genuine survey. Yet, after singling out Stalin and Trotsky, Lenin proceeded to cut both down to size. Stalin was criticized for being “too rude” and for amasing “inordinate power” as General Secretary. Lenin therefore proposed removing him from that post, though not from the top leadership, for Lenin did not intend to destroy Stalin politically, as is sometimes alleged. Lenin then evenhandedly criticized Trotsky for being drawn too much to the “administrative side of things,” which in plain language meant he was too autocratic. Even more negative remarks were directed at Zinoviev and Kamenev, whose conduct in October was labeled “no accident,” and at Bukharin, who was called a “poor Marxist.”

〔译注〕列宁《给代表大会的信》既称布哈林是重要理论家，也对其理论是否完全符合马克思主义提出保留；“蹩脚的马克思主义者”是本书作者的概括。列宁建议考虑撤换斯大林担任的具体职位是党的总书记。

zh: 于是，在这份奇特的文件中，列宁设法贬低了所有主要副手。这样做，他也许希望压低每个人的个人野心，使任何人在他去世后都无法渴望成为唯一领袖，从而避免可能分裂党的竞争。或者他可能预期自己会康复，因此试图通过强调自己仍然不可或缺来保持同事的从属地位。但无论意图如何，这份文件没有实际效果，因为他的继承者当时一致不愿照办。它只是后来被托洛茨基和布哈林的支持者挖掘出来，用以取消总书记的合法性——但那是在托洛茨基和列宁遗孀已经宣布它是伪造之后。诚然，在马克思主义列宁主义已变成的神学文化中，这份文件始终令斯大林难堪。但他的实际权力完好无损，到1929年，他已按前述方式使自己成为一个结构日益严密的党的唯一领袖。
en: Thus, in this curious document Lenin managed to denigrate all his chief lieutenants. In so doing, he may have hoped to diminish the pretensions of each one so that none could aspire to be sole leader should he die, thereby avoiding rivalries that could split the Party. Or he may have expected he was going to recover, and so sought to keep his colleagues subordinate by pointing up his own continued indispensability. But whatever his intention, the document had no practical effect because his heirs were unanimously unwilling to act on it at the time. Only later was it exhumed by the partisans of Trotsky and Bukharin to delegitimize the General Secretary—but this was after Trotsky and Lenin’s widow had already declared it to be false. To be sure, the document was always an embarrassment to Stalin in the theological culture that Marxism-Leninism had become. But his real power remained intact, and by 1929 he had made himself the sole leader of an ever more tightly structured Party, in the manner already described.

zh: 因此，对斯大林来说，1929年到了斯大林提出自己政策的时候。在反对托洛茨基和左翼反对派的斗争中，斯大林的政策在很大程度上就是布哈林的政策，但他赋予它更实用的色彩。这意味着强调“一国社会主义”的观念；这个说法布哈林已经用过，但斯大林1924年把它变成一条理论原则，向党表明它可以在国内、依靠自己完成十月任务。然而这并不意味着放弃世界革命，因为资本主义的最终推翻仍被视为苏维埃国家安全的必要条件。但它确实意味着，在此间隙，完整社会主义可以单独在俄国建成。由于当时党没有别的地方可以建设社会主义，这是对左派迷恋世界革命的巧妙反驳。
en: So, for Stalin, in 1929 the moment had arrived for policy. During the struggle against Trotsky and the Left Opposition, Stalin’s policy had been largely Bukharin’s, but he had given it a more practical cast. This meant emphasizing the idea of “socialism in one country,” a phrase that had already been used by Bukharin but which in 1924 Stalin made into a theoretical principle to indicate to the Party that it could finish the task of October at home and on its own. This did not mean rejecting world revolution, however, because the final overthrow of capitalism was still deemed necessary for the safety of the Soviet state. But it did mean that in the interval full socialism could be built in Russia alone. Since at the time the Party had nowhere else to build it, this was an astute rejoinder to the left’s infatuation with world revolution.

zh: 但斯大林直到1928—1929年才获得在俄国建设社会主义的具体纲领，而且是从他刚刚粉碎的同一个左派那里拿来的。在此之前，他并不特别关心工业化问题。甚至晚到1926年，他还反对修建巨大的第聂伯河水电站，说这就像一个农民本该用钱修犁，却愚蠢地去买留声机。只有当1928年第一个五年计划启动、工业化成为党的中心任务时，它才成为斯大林的关注中心。然而即便那时，计划也不是斯大林及其集团的产物：它源自二十年代党的一般技术官僚势头；如果说它有“派别”基础，那也是由左派以及一些前孟什维克、前社会革命党人和资产阶级专家提供的。
en: But Stalin acquired a concrete program for building socialism in Russia only in 1928-1929, and he took it from the same Left he had just crushed. Until then he had not been notably interested in problems of industrialization. Even as late as 1926 he had opposed the construction of the great Dnieprostroi Dam, saying this was like the folly of a peasant buying a gramophone when he should be using the money to repair his plow. Industrialization became central to Stalin only when it became central to the Party with the launching of the First Five-Year Plan in 1928. Even then, however, the Plan was not a product of Stalin and his group: It developed out of the general technocratic momentum of the Party in the twenties; and to the extent that it had a “factional” base, this was furnished by the Left together with various ex-Menshevik, former SR, and bourgeois specialists.

zh: 正是这个计划成为斯大林自上而下革命的载体。1928年后，他把它据为己有，并将其转变为一场第二次社会主义攻势的纲领，通向战时共产主义一种永久化、制度化的形式。正是这个被改造的计划，赋予斯大林主义的意义：它不仅是恐怖暴政或超级官僚制，而是一个总体制度。斯大林将作为成熟苏维埃秩序两大支柱——计划化和集体化——的创造者载入史册。
en: It is this Plan that was to be the vehicle for Stalin’s revolution from above. After 1928 he annexed it and transformed it into a program for a Second Socialist Offensive leading to a permanent, institutionalized version of War Communism. And it is this transformed Plan that gives us the meaning of Stalinism as not just a terroristic tyranny or a hyperbureaucracy, but as a total system. Stalin would go down in history as the creator of the two great pillars of the mature Soviet order, Planning and Collectivization.

zh: 这个在当时不仅迷住了俄国、也迷住了外部世界很大一部分的五年计划，究竟是什么？它正是历史上第一次经济计划尝试，因此标志着社会主义发展的新阶段，也标志着经济思想和实践史上的新阶段。
en: What was this Five-Year Plan that in its day mesmerized not only Russia but much of the outside world? It was nothing less than the first attempt in history at economic planning, and as such it marked a new stage in the development of socialism as well as a new stage in the history of economic thought and practice generally.

zh: 作为反对运动，古典马克思主义对资本主义的批判集中于私有财产和私人利润，以及这些制度产生的剥削之恶。它也猛烈抨击劳动分工、通过榨取剩余价值进行的资本积累，以及竞争的浪费。但它并没有把市场无政府状态，也没有把供求作为资源配置手段的盲目非理性，当作核心而明确的问题。诚然，由于私有财产、利润和货币将在社会主义下被废除，市场也必须消失，其位置必须由某种合理计划取代。但这一切都没有详细说明或强调。
en: As a movement in opposition, classical Marxism had focused its critique of capitalism on private property and private profit, and on the evil of exploitation these institutions generated. It had also inveighed against the division of labor, the accumulation of capital through the expropriation of surplus value, and the wastefulness of competition. But it had not made a central and explicit issue of the anarchy of the market, nor of the blind irrationality of supply and demand as a means of allocating resources. To be sure, since private property, profit, and money were to be abolished under socialism, the market, too, would have to disappear, and its place would have to be taken by some sort of rational planning. But none of this was spelled out in detail or emphasized.

zh: 古典马克思主义的逻辑后果，直到十九世纪末的德国经济辩论中才开始显现；正是那场辩论产生了前文提到的把资本主义视为总体体系的意识。卡尔·考茨基等社会民主党人开始思考社会主义下的计划和生活合理重组，而右翼的“讲坛社会主义者”也呼应了这种关切。这种对经济计划的关切，随后又被前文提到的鲁登道夫和拉特瑙的战争社会主义所强化。正是这种中欧横跨左派与右派的计划冲动，刺激奥地利经济学派发起了对计划的自由放任主义批判。在该学派看来，计划本质上是一项不可能的事业，因为在任何既定情况下，所需信息的数量和变量的数目都太大，无法预先计算。
正如路德维希·冯·米塞斯1920年在俄国战时共产主义的背景下所论证的，只有市场价格才能把资源配置到实际需要的地方。
en: The logical consequences of classical Marxism began to emerge only in the German economic debates of the very end of the nineteenth century that produced the already noted awareness of capitalism as a total system. Social Democrats such as Karl Kautsky began to speculate about planning and the rational reorganization of life under socialism, a concern echoed on the Right by the “Socialists of the Chair.” This concern with economic planning was then heightened by the already noted War Socialism of Ludendorff and Rathenau. And it was this Central European Left-cum-Right urge to plan that stimulated the Austrian school of economics to its laissez-faire critique of planning. In this school’s view, planning was an intrinsically impossible enterprise because in any given situation the amount of necessary information and the number of variables were too great for advance calculation.
As Ludwig von Mises argued in 1920, against the background of Russia’s War Communism, only market prices could allocate resources to where they were in fact needed.

zh: 但正是俄国马克思主义掌权的经验，才第一次充分揭示了社会主义的制度含义，而且不仅对俄国而言。战时共产主义的国有化在现代世界任何地方第一次导致市场被压制，而市场的压制又使计划的最初迹象得以出现。反过来，新经济政策的宣布使市场、而非私有财产，显得是资本主义的中心制度。接着，作为回应，1926年后第一个五年计划的起草又使计划成为社会主义的中心制度。
en: But it was the Russian experience of Marxism in power that first brought out fully the institutional implications of socialism, and not just for Russia. Nationalization under War Communism had for the first time anywhere in the modern world led to the suppression of the market, and the suppression of the market had led to the first ever intimations of planning. Conversely, the proclamation of the New Economie Policy had made the market, not private property, appear as the central institution of capitalism. Then, in answer, the drafting of the First Five-Year Plan after 1926 had made planning the central institution of socialism.

zh: 从此以后，资本主义—社会主义的对立将首先表现为市场与计划的对立；各地的人们从此把“市场经济”和“计划经济”说成这个世界上组织生活的两种可能方式。因此，苏联五年计划远不只是克服落后的工具；计划者和外部世界都把它视为创造一种全新经济秩序的试点工程。
en: From this time onward the antithesis capitalism-socialism would above all he the antithesis market-plan; people everywhere would henceforth speak of “market economies” and “planned economies” as the two possible ways of organizing life in this world. Thus the Soviet Five-Year Plan hardly appeared simply as a device for overcoming backwardness; it was viewed by both the planners and the outside world as the pilot project for creating an entirely new economic order.

zh: 然而它又不只是任何一种经济工程。计划最终源自马克思主义中圣西门主义的技术官僚传统，而这一血脉又可追溯到十八世纪的百科全书派，毕竟他们是

。这一传统相继传承：从达朗贝尔到杜尔哥，到孔多塞，到圣西门，到孔德——全都是社会工程师——再传到一般意义上的现代社会学。在这一传统的每个阶段，它都以近乎宗教的狂热坚信，对人类事务进行理性、科学的安排，可以产生一个新社会和新人类。孔多塞预言“人类绝对可完善”，或圣西门把他的技术官僚学说称为“新［世俗］基督教”，都不是偶然。特别是到圣西门和孔德时代，这一传统已采纳了这样一种信念：建立在先进技术基础上的现代工业，就是将改造人类处境的普罗米修斯；马克思完全共享这一观念。
en: Yet it was more than an economic project of any kind. The Plan derived ultimately from the Saint-Simonian technocratic strain in Marxism that in turn goes back to the eighteenth-century Encyclopedists who were, after all,

. And this strain descended in a direct succession from d’Alembert to Turgot, to Condorcet, to SaintSimon, to Comte—social engineers all—and thence to modern sociology generally. And at each stage this tradition held with an almost religious fervor that the rational, scientific ordering of human affairs could produce a new society and a new man. It was not an·accident that Condorcet predicted the “absolute perfectibility of the human race,” or that Saint-Simon called his technocratic doctrine the “New [secular] Christianity.” In particular, by the time of Saint-Simon and Comte this tradition had adopted the belief that modern industry founded on advanced technology was the Prometheus that would transform the human condition, an idea that Marx fully shared.

zh: 马克思的工业普罗米修斯主义，在俄国传统中也有其对应物：从车尔尼雪夫斯基的水晶宫，到弗拉基米尔·马雅可夫斯基的未来主义，再到尼古拉·费奥多罗夫的技术千年主义。1928年“计划”一经宣布，所有这些期待都汇聚于计划，从而在党内和整个城市社会激起了一股热情的浪潮。激进知识分子终于感到，将有一次伟大的突破，把俄国从根深蒂固的落后状态中拽出来。
en: And the industrial Prometheanism of Marx had its counterpart in a Russian tradition that led from Chernyshevskii’s crystal palace to Vladimir Mayakovskii’s futurism and Nikolai Fedorov’s technological millenarianism. All of these currents of expectation attached themselves to the Plan once it was proclaimed in 1928 and so produced a groundswell of emotion within the Party and in urban society generally. At last, the radical intelligentsia felt, there would be a great breakthrough to wrest Russia from her inveterate backwardness.

zh: 这股热情还承载着对落后堡垒——即“愚昧的人们”、未开化的俄国农民——的巨大敌意。农民在俄国社会中一向居于中心位置（他们占人口的绝大多数），在俄罗斯民族神话中也同样如此。自从彼得打开他著名的通往欧洲的窗户以来，俄国在文化上便一分为二：一边是欧化的、世俗的贵族和知识分子，另一边是仍保留莫斯科公国时代文化、信奉东正教的农民。取决于立足点不同，这可以意味着上层阶级已经变得像外国人一样，只有农民才是真正的俄国人；也可以意味着贵族和知识分子是理性与进步的力量，而农民则是亚洲式野蛮、迷信和停滞的沉重负担。
en: This surge of enthusiasm also carried a great charge of hostility toward that bastion of backwardness—the “dark people,” the benighted Russian peasants. The peasants had always occupied a central place in Russian society—where they constituted the overwhelming majority—as well as in the Russian national mythology. Ever since Peter cut his famous window through to Europe, Russia, culturally speaking, had been divided into two: the Europeanized and secular gentry and intelligentsia on the one hand, and the still Muscovite and Orthodox peasantry on the other. Depending on one’s point of view, this could mean that the upper classes had become foreign and the peasants alone were the true Russians; or it could mean that the gentry and intelligentsia were the force for rationality and progress, and the peasants were a dead weight of Asiatic barbarism, superstition, and stagnation.

zh: 这两种视角与1840年代斯拉夫派和西方派两个阵营初现时的分歧大有关系。后来，陀思妥耶夫斯基成为前一种观点的极端例子，而列宁，如我们已经看到的，是后一种立场的更极端代表。但对两个阵营来说，农民在界定俄国意义方面所起的作用，在其他欧洲大国的农村阶层中找不到对应——即便像1789年的法国那样（或者就19世纪欧洲大部分地区而言），这些农民占人口的80%。因此，既然“计划”承诺要终结农民在俄国生活中的优势地位，它也就提出要对民族进行彻底重新定义。在这个意义上，它是革命西方主义的一项举措，是俄国最终欧洲化的杠杆。
en: These two perspectives had much to do with the differences between the Slavophiles and the Westernizers when the two camps first emerged in the 1840s, Later, Dostoevsky would be an extreme example of the former view, and Lenin, as we have seen, an even more extreme representative of the latter position. But for both camps, the peasantry defined the meaning of Russia in a manner that the rural classes defined no other major European nation—even when, as in the France of 1789 (or in most of nineteenth-century Europe, for that matter) these peasants constituted 80 percent of the population. Thus, since the Plan promised to end the preponderance of the peasantry in Russian life, it also proposed a radical redefinition of the nation. In this sense it was a measure of revolutionary Westernism, the lever for the ultimate Europeanization of Russia.

zh: 党当然不会用这些传统俄国的说法来表述，但它的马克思主义范畴表达了类似的东西；事实上，它们还增添了一股致命的新力量，因为按其正式教义，马克思主义从根本上激烈地反对农民。我们在战时共产主义期间已经看到这一点付诸行动；在第一个五年计划期间，它将充分凸显出来。
en: The Party, of course, did not put matters in these conventionally Russian terms, but its Marxist categories expressed something similar; indeed, they added a lethal new charge, for in its formal tenets Marxism is fundamentally and aggressively antipeasant. We have already seen this in action during War Communism; it would come fully to the fore during the First Five-Year Plan.

zh: 用马克思主义的话说，农民不只是效率低下的生产者，必须设法把他们带入现代性。相反，他们是一个无可救药地古老的阶级，被历史的逻辑判定要消亡，确切地说是要被“消灭”。当马克思用“消灭”一词来描述应当如何对待农村生活的愚昧，或捷克人这类无可救药地落后的民族时，他并不是指肉体灭绝：对农民，他指的是城市化；对捷克人，他指的是德意志化；但在这两种情况下，他指的都是整个群体作为群体的消失。诚然，列宁曾把农民中的较贫困阶层从马克思对农村的总体谴责中豁免出来；但他这样做基本上是出于策略和暂时的理由。
en: In Marxist terms the peasants are not just inefficient producers who must somehow be brought into modernity. Rather, they are a hopelessly archaic class condemned by the logic of history to extinction, indeed to “liquidation.” Now, when Marx used the word “liquidation” to describe what needed to be done to the idiocy of rural life or to hopelessly retrograde nations such as the Czechs, he did not mean physical extermination: he meant urbanization in the case of the peasants, and Germanization in the case of the Czechs, but in both cases he meant the elimination of entire groups. To be sure, Lenin had exempted the poorer stratum of the peasantry from Marx’s global condemnation of the village; but he did so essentially on tactical and temporary grounds.

zh: 此外，在马克思主义中，历史的逻辑是由阶级斗争驱动的；因此，农民将通过一场经济斗争而被文明化和城市化，这场斗争最终将以他们的消失告终。英国农民在资本主义兴起过程中被资产阶级如此处置，正是这样的命运；马克思虽然痛斥那些资产阶级剥削者，却也坚定地认为他们的行为是必要而进步的，因为它是通向社会主义的逻辑的一部分。
最后，马克思主义认为，世界上所有较为落后的民族都必须走这条痛苦的欧洲道路。
en: In Marxism, moreover, the logic of history was driven by the class war; it followed, therefore, that the peasants would be civilized and urbanized by means of an economic struggle that would culminate in their elimination. This indeed had been the fate of the English peasantry at the hands of the bourgeoisie during the emergence of capitalism, and although Marx excoriated those bourgeois exploiters, he also firmly held that their action was necessary and progressive because it was part of the logic leading to socialism.
Finally, Marxism held that all of the more backward nations of the world would have to follow this painful European path.

zh: 如我们所见，这整套思维方式是俄国计划争论的组成部分。因此，通过阶级斗争消灭农民，既是“计划”的前提，也是它的最终含义，无论计划所要求的集体化实际百分比是多少。因为“计划”实际上提出要终结“城乡分工”——对马克思主义者来说，这是人类异化的第一种、也是最基本的形式。
en: This whole mode of thinking, as we have seen, was integral to the planning debate in Russia. Thus elimination of the peasantry through class struggle was both a premise and a final implication of the Plan, whatever the actual percentage of collectivization it called for. For in effect the Plan proposed to end the “division of labor between town and country” that was the first and most basic form of human alienation for Marxists.

zh: 诚然，斯大林并不是用这些说法向党和全国力陈其总路线的。然而，这条总路线潜意识地借用了俄国文化中的西方化传统，并且相当明确地借用了马克思主义观点，即一切政治都是阶级斗争，历史最终在社会主义中获得解决。只有在这样一种末世论的语境中，第一个五年计划的疯狂豪赌才可理解。因为再怎么强调也不为过：布尔什维克并不只是要发展一个落后国家；他们要建设社会主义。
en: To be sure, these were not the terms Stalin used to urge his General Line on the Party and the country. Nonetheless, that General Line drew subliminally on the Westernizing tradition in Russian culture, and it drew quite explicitly on the Marxist view that all politics is class struggle culminating in the final resolution of history in socialism. It is only in the context of this eschatology that the mad wager of the First Five-Year Plan is comprehensible. For it cannot be emphasized enough that the Bolsheviks were not just out to develop a backward country; they were out to build socialism.

zh: 1929年4月最终通过的“计划”，试图把这些总体目标“科学地”转化为农业和工业的精确数量指标。这样做的方法已经酝酿了好几年。1924年，国家计划委员会开始发布下一年的“控制数字”或预测。1925年，它开始起草未来发展的实际计划。1926年，当战后恢复大体完成时，为未来工业扩张制订计划变得紧迫起来。到1927年，扩张已经在进行，因此党在第十五次代表大会上，在开除左派的同时，通过了左派的纲领，从而责成国家计划委员会起草五年计划。事实上，对这一纲领的支持已变得如此普遍，以致后来作为斯大林建设社会主义手段而载入史册的这个“计划”，最初是由布哈林和李可夫向代表大会提出的。
en: The Plan as finally adopted in April 1929 attempted to translate “scientifically” these general goals into precise quantitative targets for agriculture and industry. The methods for doing this had been several years in gestation. In 1924 Gosplan had begun to publish “control figures,” or projections, for the coming year. In 1925 it started drafting actual plans for future development. In 1926, when the postwar recovery was largely completed, this planning for future industrial expansion became urgent. By 1927 expansion was already underway, so the Party at its Fifteenth Congress, at the same time that it expelled the Left, adopted the Left’s program and thus charged Gosplan with drawing up a Five-Year Plan. Indeed, so universal had support for this program now become that the Plan which would go down in history as Stalin’s means of building socialism was first sponsored before the Congress by Bukharin and Rykov.

zh: 代表大会还决定，党在农村的目标不应是列宁那些微不足道的合作社，而应是真正的集体农庄。而且恰在此时，“采购危机”袭来，这使集体化和工业化都更加紧迫。1928年间，紧迫感与党内的兴奋情绪融合在一起，因为一场新的社会主义进攻有望最终结束新经济政策带来的屈辱和妥协。到1929年初，这种情绪产生了一个“计划”（其起始日期很不科学地回溯到1928年10月1日），远远超出了左派当年提出的任何方案。
en: The Congress also decided that the Party’s goal in the countryside should not be Lenin’s puny cooperatives but real collective farms. Just at this point, moreover, the “procurements crisis” hit, and this gave an added urgency to both collectivization and industrialization. In the course of 1928, urgency was fused with exhilaration within the Party at the prospect of a new Socialist Offensive that would at last put an end to the humiliations and compromises of the NEP. And this mood by early 1929 produced a Plan (whose beginning was quite unscientifically backdated to October 1, 1928) that went far beyond anything the Left had proposed in its day.

zh: 结果产生了一个即便对城市尚未缺粮的国家也过于乐观的纲领。“计划”的前提假设是工业与农业将同步扩张，一方的增长为另一方的增长提供养料。而且在工业部门内部，重工业和轻工业要齐头并进。也就是说，投资与消费要同时增长：国家的资本存量要成倍增加，与此同时人民要生活得更好，工人和农民平等受益。此外，“计划”还以“初步”和“最佳”两个版本提交给党，党当然选择了后者。例如，那个版本预计到1933年铁矿石产量将增长233%，钢产量增长160%，而国民收入将增长506%！
en: The result was a program that would have been over-optimistic even for a country whose cities were not already running short of food. The Plan was predicated on the assumption that industry and agriculture would expand in tandem, with growth in one feeding growth in the other. Within the industrial sector, moreover, both heavy and light industry were to advance together. Thus investment and consumption were to increase simultaneously: The capital stock of the country was to multiply, while at the same time people would live better, with the worker and the peasant benefiting equally. In addition, the Plan was proposed to the Party in an “initial” and an “optimal” variant, and of course the Party chose the latter. That version anticipated, for example, that by 1933 the production of iron ore would increase 233 percent, and that of steel 160 percent, while national income would go up 506 percent!

zh: 人们常常论证说，最初通过的计划虽然在若干预测上有所夸大，但整体上并非不切实际，尤其考虑到1933年实现15%集体化这一温和目标。这种观点还认为，如果说计划出了偏差，那是因为斯大林的干预使它变了质。
但这种对计划的评估值得怀疑：当时的数据根本不足以产生计划所伪称的那种精确性。此外，对如此长达五年、涵盖经济每一个方面的预测性规划，还存在严肃的理论异议；事实上，经过几十年的尝试，从未有任何苏联式经济成功制订出一份它真正能够执行的计划。正是出于这些原因，并且为了回应斯大林和奥地利学派，当时一些较为谨慎的西方社会主义者提出了市场社会主义这一混合替代方案——一个尚待实践的理论概念。
en: It has often been argued that the Plan as first adopted, though inflated in some of its projections, was nonetheless not unrealistic as a whole, particularly in view of the modest target of 15 percent collectivization by 1933. This view also holds that if the Plan went awry, it was because Stalin’s interference denatured it.

But this assessment of the Plan is doubtful: The data were simply insufficient at the time to produce anything like the precision to which the Plan pretended. Then there are serious theoretical objections to projective planning for so long a period as five years, and for every aspect of the economy; in fact, during decades of trying, no Soviet-type economy has ever succeeded in producing a plan it could actually carry out. It is for reasons such as these, and in answer to both Stalin and the Austrians, that some of the more cautious Western socialists at the time came up with the hybrid alternative of market socialism—a theoretical concept yet to be realized in practice.

zh: 因此，即便在斯大林掌控它之前，最好把“计划”理解为技术官僚乌托邦主义的一次狂想，它诞生于俄国当时面临的真实发展问题与刚才提到的意识形态思潮的结合。起初，斯大林及其手下既在煽动这股技术官僚冲动，也在乘势利用它。然后他们介入进来，把这种冲动变成了一场猛攻。
en: Thus the Plan, even before Stalin got hold of it, is best understood as a flight of technocratic utopianism born of a conjunction of the genuine development problems Russia then faced and the ideological currents just mentioned. At the beginning, Stalin and his men rode this technocratic impetus as much as they incited it. Then they stepped in and transformed the impetus into an onslaught.

zh: 斯大林所做的是接管这个意在体现技术官僚理性的事业的政治领导权。具体而言，这意味着把经济计划与一场政治—军事运动联系起来，通过强制性和全面集体化来结束采购危机；而这又意味着通过不断加快发展的“速度”，使工业计划政治化和军事化。这个改造计划的过程由斯大林及其集团在1928—1929年间实施。由于这一过程遭到“右派”抵制，它便成了消灭该派别的契机。
en: What Stalin did was to take over the political management of this would-be technocratic enterprise. Concretely, this meant linking the economic Plan with a political-military campaign to end the procurements crisis through forced and total collectivization; and this in turn meant politicizing and militarizing the industrial plan by constantly accelerating its “tempos” of development. This process of transforming the Plan was carried out by Stalin and his group during the period 1928-1929. And because the process was resisted by the “Right,” it became the occasion for that faction’s elimination.

zh: 终极阶级斗争
en: THE ULTIMATE CLASS STRUGGLE

zh: （“这是最后的斗争”）

zh: 第一个五年计划所创造的斯大林主义体系，其意义只能通过一连串在行动与反应中展开、并生成新秩序的事件来理解。尽管斯大林及其手下是在一个“计划”的框架内行事，他们并没有宏伟蓝图，甚至没有一份大致成形的纲领草案，也没有任何关于如何实施的清晰想法。他们只有社会主义这一总体目标，被理解为有计划的工业化和全面集体化。在这些总体目标的范围内，他们即兴制定具体纲领，但结果却出乎他们的预料。因此，党发动第二场俄国革命的方式，与它当初启动战时共产主义和新经济政策的方式相同：它迈出最初看似有限的一步，由此启动的进程迅速获得了自身的发展势头；于是，为防止整个攻势失败，一桩罪行又促使他们犯下另一桩罪行。
en: The meaning of the Stalinist system created by the First Five-Year Plan can only be understood in terms of the succession of events, unfolding through action and reaction, that generated the new order. Despite the fact that Stalin and his men were operating in the context of a “Plan,” they had no grand design, or even an approximate draft of a program, or any clear idea of how to implement it. Instead, they had only the general goal of socialism understood as planned industrialization and full collectivization. Within these parameters they improvised their concrete program, but with results they had never anticipated. So the Party unleashed the Second Russian Revolution in the same way that it had initiated War Communism and the NEP: It took a first, apparently limited, step, and the process thus initiated quickly acquired a momentum of its own; hence one crime necessitated another in order to stave off defeat of the entire Offensive.

zh: 这一进程始于1927年12月著名的粮食采购短缺。斯大林于1928年1月立即作出反应，其举动近乎一场党内政变。在获得政治局批准进行一次有限的紧急粮食征收后，斯大林发动了一场大规模的余粮征集制运动：他和几位主要副手——莫洛托夫、卡冈诺维奇、日丹诺夫、安德烈耶夫——分赴据称富农囤积余粮的地区，用战时共产主义的手段向他们勒索粮食。由于斯大林在这次运动中亲自督战乌拉尔和西西伯利亚，这种新版的余粮征集制便被称为“乌拉尔—西伯利亚方法”。
en: This process began with the famous shortfall in grain procurements of December 1927. Stalin immediately responded in January 1928 with what came close to being an intra-Party coup d’état. After obtaining approval of the Politbro for a limited, emergency collection of grain, Stalin mounted a major campaign of

: he and some of his chief lieutenants—Molotov, Kaganovich, Zhdanov, Andreev—fanned out to the regions where kulaks were allegedly hoarding a surplus and extorted it from them through the methods of War Communism. Because Stalin personally worked over the Urals and Western Siberia during this campaign, this new version of
came to be known as the “Urals-Siberian method.”

zh: 这场运动奏效了：农民被吓住了，粮食被收上来了。当布哈林及其盟友反对说这威胁到工农联盟（
）时，斯大林退让了，说这只是一项紧急措施，不是新的方针。然而先例已经树立，斯大林在1928年晚些时候和1929年再次诉诸这一办法，以支持刚刚通过的计划。不过，每次收集到的粮食都很有限。显然，这种方法只能是一时的权宜之计，不能解决长期供养城市和红军的难题。因此，斯大林决定一劳永逸地解决粮食问题：把乌拉尔—西伯利亚方法用于实现全国立即全面集体化。
en: And the campaign worked: The peasants were cowed, the grain was collected. When Bukharin and his allies objected that this threatened the

, Stalin backed off and said it was only an emergency measure, not a new departure. A precedent had nonetheless been set, and Stalin returned to it later in 1928 and again in 1929 to back up the Plan that had just been adopted. Still, only minimal quantities of grain were collected each time. Such a method, clearly, could only be a temporary expedient, not a solution to the long-term dilemma of feeding the cities and the Red Army. Stalin therefore decided to solve the grain problem definitively by applying the Urals-Siberian method to achieve full and immediate collectivization of the entire country.

zh: 但只有在其他战线得到保障之后，才能把这一意图付诸行动。首先，工业化运动可能面临由资产阶级专家变成“破坏分子”所带来的问题。为了警告这些不可或缺却又可疑的助手——无论是俄国人还是外国人——1928年春，来自乌克兰沙赫特矿区的大约五十名工程师因替国际资本从事破坏活动而受到公审。公诉人是安德烈·维辛斯基；所有被告都认罪，五人被处决。沙赫特事件事实上扰乱了工业化，但它仍然产生了政治效果：让工人们看到，他们的悲惨处境是阶级敌人无休止阴谋造成的；因此，警惕和斗争也必须永无止境。这一事件由此创立了一个公式，将被反复使用，直到1936—1938年大清洗的宏大高潮
——届时维辛斯基再次担任公诉人。
en: But it would be possible to act on this intention only once other fronts had been secured. First, the industrialization drive might face problems arising from bourgeois specialists turned “wreckers.” As a warning to these indispensable yet dubious aides, both Russian and foreign, in the spring of 1928 some fifty engineers from the Ukrainian mining region of Shakhty were given a show trial for sabotage in the service of international capital. The prosecutor was Andrei Vyshinskii; all of the accused confessed, and five were executed. Although the Shakhty affair in fact disrupted industrialization, it nonetheless had the political effect of showing the workers that their miserable plight was due to the never-ending machinations of class enemies; accordingly, vigilance and struggle must also be unending. The affair thus created a formula that would be repeated until the grand crescendo of the Purges of 1936-1938
—when Vyshinskii again was prosecutor.

zh: 与此同时，党本身也必须得到保障。布哈林此时虽然可以接受通过财政手段对农民进行“某种挤压”，以及在必要时偶尔诉诸乌拉尔—西伯利亚方法，但不能指望他同意强制集体化；总理李可夫和工会领袖托姆斯基也持同样态度。正如我们所见，正是因为这个原因，布哈林及其盟友被扣上“右派”的帽子，并在次年既被解除党内职务，又被解除国家职务。
en: At the same time, the Party itself had to be secured. Although Bukharin would now accept “some squeeze” on the peasants through fiscal means and occasional emergency resort to the Urals-Siberian method, he could not be counted on to agree to forced collectivization, an attitude shared by Prime Minister Rykov and trade union chief Tomskii, It was for this reason, as we have seen, that Bukharin and his allies were branded as the “Right.” and that the next year they were removed from both their Party and state posts.

zh: 这使斯大林第一次拥有一个完全由自己人组成的政治局，以及一个同质性只稍逊一筹的中央委员会。这也使他第一次直接控制国家机器。诚然，所有国家领导人物一向都是优秀的党员。但当莫洛托夫取代李可夫出任总理，当一个斯大林主义委员会取代相对独立的托姆斯基时，这两个封地便直接隶属于领袖了。与此同时，计划机构开始失去其准自治性：古比雪夫领导下的最高国民经济委员会——他当然得到斯大林的支持——在1928年初之后向国家计划委员会施压，要求它把预测激进化：结果是对计划的期望从大胆的“初步”版本升级为乌托邦式的“最佳”版本。于是，前孟什维克计划人员开始觉得，他们的谨慎可能被解释为破坏，因而不敢公开表达自己的担忧；而斯大林则真心认为，一切温和的建议都带有小资产阶级嫌疑，因此可以放心忽视。事态就这样不断升级，最终连最佳计划也被超过。
en: This gave Stalin for the first time a Politbro composed entirely of his own men, and a Central Committee only slightly less homogeneous. It also gave him for the first time direct control of the state apparatus. To be sure, all state leaders had always been good Party men. But when Molotov replaced Rykov as Prime Minister, and when a Stalinist committee took over from the relatively independent Tomskii, these two fiefs were directly subordinated to the Leader. At the same time, the planning apparatus began to lose its quasi autonomy as Vesenkha under Kuibyshev—who was of course supported by Stalin—pressured Gosplan after early 1928 to radicalize its projections: The result was the escalation of expectations from the bold “initial” to the Utopian “optimal” variant of the Plan. In consequence, ex-Menshevik planners began to feel that their prudence could be construed as sabotage and hence muted their alarm, while Stalin genuinely believed that all moderate advice was suspect as petty bourgeois and thus could safely be ignored. And so matters spiralled toward surpassing even the optimal Plan.

zh: 最后，意识形态也得到修订，以为即将到来的攻势提供正当理由。斯大林宣称，国家离社会主义越近，阶级敌人的抵抗就越强，阶级斗争就越激烈。这个理论常被讥笑为低劣的马克思主义（因而又成了斯大林背叛列宁遗产的又一证据），因为按照逻辑，随着社会主义胜利临近，阶级斗争应当减弱。这一批评可以追溯到1920年代的辩论（布哈林称斯大林的观点是“白痴般的无知”）；就马克思主义的正式教义而言，它是正确的——而这恰恰是它的问题所在。因为这种批评预设了按字面接受马克思关于通向社会主义的历史逻辑的设想；而这种对意识形态的字面忠诚，只会遮蔽意识形态在历史中实际运作的方式。
en: Finally, ideology was revised to justify the coming offensive. Stalin declared that the nearer the country got to socialism, the stronger the resistance of the class enemy became and the more intense the class struggle grew. This theory has often been ridiculed as debased Marxism (and thus still another proof that Stalin betrayed the legacy of Lenin) since the class struggle should logically abate as the victory of socialism approaches. This criticism, which goes back to the debates of the 1920s (Bukharin called Stalin’s view “idiotic ignorance”), is correct in terms of Marxism’s formal tenets—and this is precisely what is wrong with it. For such criticism presupposes a literal-minded acceptance of Marx’s vision of the historical logic leading to socialism; and such literal commitment to ideology can only obscure the way ideology in fact operates in history.

zh: 1929年党所面对的困境是：现实中的历史并不符合它假定的逻辑，但党作为一个意识形态统治的政权，仍然不可更改地致力于遵循这一逻辑。因此，马克思的学说只能沦为党的理性的乖戾狡计之牺牲品。因为当时俄国并不存在阶级斗争，存在的只是党对以农民为主体的民族所进行的斗争；于是马克思的理论被用来为一个强制性的五年计划提供正当理由，而该计划旨在完善党的权力。事实上，历史真正的逻辑或许内在地决定了：意识形态一旦与政治行动接触，几乎总会发生变质；意识形态的抱负越高，所设想的行动越剧烈，实践中的贬低就越可能发生。斯大林那个备受讥笑的理论，正是通过这条迂回的道路，创造性地把马克思主义关于阶级斗争的首要原则改编为党在绝境中的政策，从而使它成为建设苏维埃社会主义的首要原则。
en: The dilemma confronting the Party in 1929 was that history does not in reality conform to its presumed logic, yet the Party as an ideocratic regime was irrevocably committed to following this logic nonetheless. Marx’s doctrine therefore could only fall victim to the perverse cunning of Party reason. For there was no class struggle in Russia at the time, but only a struggle of the Party against the peasant nation; thus Marx’s theory was made to serve as justification for a coercive Five-Year Plan designed to perfect the Party’s power. Indeed, it is perhaps inherent in the real logic of history that ideologies are almost invariably debased on contact with political action; the higher the ambition of the ideology, and the more drastic the contemplated action, the more likely is the debasement in practice. By this devious route Stalin’s much derided theorem in fact creatively adapted the cardinal Marxist principle of the class struggle to desperate Party policy, thereby making it the cardinal principle of the building of Soviet socialism.

zh: 因为斯大林定理的实际含义相当清楚：国家离集体化越近，就可以预期农民抵抗得越厉害；工业化越是被强行推进，就越可能发生危机，而这些危机最好通过归咎于资产阶级专家的破坏来克服。既然政权正准备使用强制手段，那么它也准备应对强烈反应、并因此准备进一步强制，在他们看来也就是审慎之举。因此，斯大林的新意识形态立场意在为即将到来的社会战争进行心理动员。
en: For the practical meaning of Stalin’s theorem was quite clear: The nearer the country got to collectivization, the more strongly the peasants could be expected to resist; and the more industrialization was forced, the more likely was the occurrence of crises that were best overcome by blaming them on the sabotage of bourgeois specialists. Since the regime was preparing to use coercion, it was only prudent for it to prepare also for strong action in response and thus for further coercion. Stalin’s new ideological stance was thus intended as psychological mobilization for the coming social war.

zh: 但使斯大林的新路线成为可能的决定性因素，是他运用乌拉尔—西伯利亚方法的经验。党尝试了强制手段，而且奏效了：农民没有反击，国家也没有像胆怯的“右派”所预言的那样陷入战时共产主义的混乱。于是斯大林断定，如果党的机器施加巨大而持续的压力，分散在全国各地小单位中的农民将无法进行有效抵抗。正是这个重大误判，把计划的集体化运动变成了一场政权与农民之间的战争。
en: But the decisive factor in making possible Stalin’s new course was his experience with the Urals-Siberian method. The Party had tried coercion and it worked: The peasants did not fight back, and the country was not plunged into the disorder of War Communism, as timorous “Rightists” had predicted. So Stalin concluded that if the Party machine applied massive, sustained pressure, the peasants, dispersed in small units across the country, would be incapable of offering serious resistance. And it is this great miscalculation that turned the Plan’s collectivization drive into a war between the regime and the peasants.

zh: 系统性的压力始于1929年夏天，当时斯大林的主要副手秘密带领党的积极分子在选定地区试行大规模集体化，采用任何看来合适的手段。结果，到10月1日，集体农庄（kolkhoz）成员从大约一百万人增加到两百万人。斯大林随后宣称，这证明“中农”已被争取到社会主义事业一边，正自愿地、大批地加入集体农庄。他由此可以把党的自上而下的革命说成是对来自下层的压力的回应；而且他很可能对自己宣传的相当一部分信以为真。
en: Systematic pressure began in the summer of 1929, when Stalin’s chief aides secretly led Party activists in trying out mass collectivization in selected areas and by whatever means seemed appropriate. In consequence, by October 1 collective-farm, or kolkhoz, membership has increased from approximately one million to two million. Stalin then alleged that this was proof that the “middle peasants” had been won over to the cause of socialism and were entering the kolkhozes voluntarily and en masse. He could thus present the Party’s revolution from above as a response to pressure from below; and he may well have believed a good part of his own propaganda.

zh: 因为一个令人吃惊的事实是，自1928年1月那次乌拉尔—西伯利亚地区之行以后，斯大林再也没有访问过俄国农村。在整个集体化运动期间，事实上直到他生命的终点，他从未视察过任何一个红色集体农庄；他与面带微笑的农妇合影，纯粹是摆拍。斯大林只通过富农、中农和贫农这些意识形态范畴来看待俄国农村。的确，他几乎不曾去看过作为计划重点的新城市和工业俄国，甚至在第二次世界大战的极端紧急状态中，他唯一一次前线之行也是一次匆忙的官方活动。
en: For it is a startling fact that after his foray into the Urals-Siberian region in January 1928, Stalin never visited rural Russia again. Throughout the whole collectivization drive, in fact to the end of his days, he never inspected a Red kolkhoz; the photographs of him with smiling peasant women were purely staged affairs. Stalin saw rural Russia only through the ideological categories of kulak, middle, and poor peasant. Indeed, he hardly looked in on the new urban and industrial Russia that was the Plan’s focus, and even during the supreme emergency of the Second World War his one visit to the front was a hasty, official event.

zh: 从1928年起，斯大林完全在党的领地内统治俄国、建设社会主义：克里姆林宫附近老广场上的中央委员会总部，以及克里姆林宫本身的政府大院。到1930年，他的主要基地——书记处——已成为一个名副其实的党中之党；它下设六个部，监督普通党员并监管一切政府活动。此外，在二十年代末，斯大林设立了由亚历山大·波斯克列贝舍夫领导的私人秘书处，其成员包括未来的政治警察首脑尼古拉·叶若夫之类阴森的人物。他从这些莫斯科堡垒中外出，只到昆采沃的郊外别墅“近郊”（Blizhnii），夏天则到克里米亚或黑海沿岸索契同样戒备森严的休养地。他与真实的国家隔绝，只能通过党的报告和政策来看待它。难怪，当他发动第二次攻势时，他真以为自己能用一记闪电战取胜。
en: From 1928 on, Stalin ruled Russia and built socialism entirely from within the Party precincts in Central Committee headquarters on Old Square, down a side street from the Kremlin, and in the governmental compound of the Kremlin itself. By 1930 his primary base, the Secretariat, had become a veritable party within the Party; with its six departments it monitored the ordinary membership and oversaw all governmental activity. In addition, at the end of the twenties, Stalin created a personal secretariat under Aleksandr Poskrebyshev and staffed with such sinister creatures as the future head of the political police, Nikolai Ezhov. From these Muscovite fortresses he ventured forth only to his suburban villa of “Nearby” (“Blizhnii”) at Kuntsevo, and in summer to equally guarded retreats in the Crimea or at Sochi on the Black Sea. Cut off from the real country, he saw it only through the eyes of Party reports and policy. Small wonder, then, that when he started the Second Offensive he really believed he could win it with a lightning stroke.

zh: 于是，在11月7日革命十二周年纪念日的讲话中，斯大林宣布1929年是“大转折之年”，国家已准备好“全速前进”奔向社会主义。这很快也意味着大规模或全面（
）集体化的目标。但对农业计划的这一修订必然也要求对工业计划作出修订，因此党在12月宣布，五年计划的目标将在四年内实现。斯大林由此表明，国家正在开始第二场革命。
en: Thus, on November 7, in his address on the twelfth anniversary of the Revolution, Stalin declared that 1929 had been “the year of the Great Break” and that the country was ready to advance “full steam ahead” to socialism. And this soon meant also the goal of mass or total (

) collectivization. But this revision of the Plan for agriculture necessarily entailed a revision for industry as well, so in December the Party proclaimed that the goals of the Five-Year Plan were to be achieved in four years. Stalin thus made it clear that the country was embarking on a Second Revolution.

zh: 为了增强这一时刻的象征意义，12月21日，他的五十岁生日以十足的党内排场加以庆祝。他由此从“老板”（
，这是他此前严格的党内角色）转变为“领袖”（
，这是他从此担当的全国性的角色）。于是他开始了作为“今天的列宁”的生涯。明确的信息是：列宁完成了第一场革命，即十月革命；斯大林现在将完成第二场、也是最后一场革命，以真正建成社会主义。党在二十年代精心构建、实际上也是党对自身崇拜的列宁崇拜，已经创造了全知领袖的范本；
斯大林只需步入这个角色。到1929年12月底，苏维埃大跃进所需的一切要素都已齐备。进攻可以开始了。
en: To heighten the symbolism of the occasion, on December 21 his fiftieth birthday was celebrated with full Party pomp. He was thus transformed from Boss (
), his strictly Party role hitherto, into Leader (

), his national role henceforth. Thus he began his career as the “Lenin of today.” The clear message was that Lenin had made the first, October Revolution, and that Stalin would now make the second and final revolution for the actual building of socialism. The Lenin cult, elaborated in the twenties as the Party’s cult of itself, had already created the model of the all-wise Leader;
Stalin had only to step into the role. By the end of December 1929, all the elements necessary for the Soviet great leap forward had been assembled. The attack could begin.

zh: 用当时的军事术语来说，这场运动在两条主要“战线”——农业和工业——上展开。每一条战线内部又有许多分战线：例如小麦战线和棉花战线，煤炭战线和钢铁战线。此外还有第三条大战线：“文化”。这指的是消除文盲现象、技术无知，以及早先让列宁深感困扰的那种普遍的
（nekulturnost），或者说未经现代文明改造的俄国对现代生活的整体无能——这些特征显然首先与
（庄稼汉）联系在一起。而且，在所有这些战线上，如果出现瓶颈或其他不可预见的意外，解决办法就是投入“突击队”；
，即突击工人，成为工人阶级中最高的荣誉头衔之一。同样，工人小组被号召参加“社会主义竞赛”，以心理手段提高生产，因为物质激励无法提供。
en: To use the military terminology of the day, the campaign unfolded on two major “fronts,” agriculture and industry. Within each of these there were numerous subfronts: the wheat front and the cotton front, for example, and the coal front and the steel front. Then there was a third great front, “culture.” By this was meant the war against illiteracy, technological ignorance, and that general
which had earlier so bothered Lenin, or raw Russia’s overall ineptitude for modern life—characteristics that were obviously associated above all with the
. On any of these fronts, moreover, if there was a bottleneck or other unforeseen contingency, the problem was to be met by throwing in “shock brigades”;

, or shock worker, became one of the highest titles of honor among the working class. In similar fashion, groups of workers were called on to compete in contests of “socialist emulation,” to raise production by psychological means, since material incentives could not be offered.

zh: 既然有战线，也就必然有敌人。其中首要的当然是富农。但还有其他种类的敌人：耐普曼、投机者、在国家计划委员会工作或担任工程师的资产阶级专家、仍留在党内的右翼和左翼偏离分子；所有这些人都可能变成“破坏分子”，都可能与外国“帝国主义者”接触。因此，每条战线上的斗争都必须以相应的阶级“警惕性”和阶级斗争精神来进行。
en: And if there are fronts, there must also be enemies. The principal of these, of course, was the kulak. But there were also other species of enemy: nepmen, speculators, bourgeois specialists working in Gosplan or as engineers, Right- and Left-wing deviationists still in the Party; all of these might turn into “wreckers,” and all might enter into contact with foreign “imperialists.” So the struggle on each front had to be conducted with appropriate class “vigilance” and in a spirit of class warfare.

zh: 而且，每条战线上的斗争都被认为与其他所有战线有机相连，任何一条战线的失败都被认为可能危及整场战争。正是这种对伟大社会主义进攻的全局性或总体性信念，部分解释了它在1930年1月开始时的仓促和毫无准备。尤其是，一旦工业化的速度在1929年底被急剧加快，党的领导层便确信，除非立即把农民集体化，否则到1931年工业战线将因缺乏足够粮食供应而崩溃。这一情况使农业战线在攻势开始时成为首要任务。
en: The struggle on each front was, moreover, perceived as organically linked to all the others, and failure in any one was believed to threaten defeat in the whole war. It is this belief in the global or total nature of the Great Socialist Offensive that explains in part the haste and unpreparedness with which it began in January 1930. In particular, once the tempo of industrialization had been radically accelerated at the end of 1929, the Party leadership was convinced that unless the peasants were collectivized immediately, the industrial front would collapse by 1931 for want of an adequate food supply. And this circumstance made the agricultural front the chief priority as the offensive began.

zh: 因此，大跃进的第一步，是在1930年1月宣布“把富农作为一个阶级加以消灭”。党的积极分子工作队、工人营、共青团学生以及国家政治保卫局（GPU，契卡的继承机构）的支队被派往各村。在这些群体中，最著名的是“两万五千人队”，由党的工作者组成，他们的热情可以使集体化运动看起来像是无产阶级的自发行动。

这些群体的表面任务是与贫农“结盟”，把富农逐出村庄，并争取中农支持集体农庄。事实上，这些一向含糊的词语现在完全失去了意义。真正发生的是整个村庄被强行置于党的统治之下：“富农”变得仅仅意味着任何抗拒集体化的庄稼汉，因此就成了“敌人”。党的工作者在更贫困的农民帮助下，径行剥夺这些“富农”的土地和牲畜，要么把他们抛到乡间流浪，要么——更常见的是——把他们塞进货运车厢，流放到北方；因为从前的“富农”不允许加入新的集体农庄。据政治局的数据，在集体化过程中，约有五百万到六百万人被“去富农化”。1930年运动的战术原则是出其不意地拿下农民，在抵抗组织起来之前分化村庄，从而在春播前完成全部工作。
en: Accordingly, the first step of the Great Leap was to proclaim, in January 1930, the “liquidation of the kulaks as a class.” Brigades of Parry activists, worker battalions, Komsomol students, and detachments from the GPU (as the Cheka was now known) were dispatched to the villages. Among these groups the most famous was the Twenty-Five Thousanders, which consisted of Party workers whose zeal could make the collectivization drive appear as a spontaneous initiative of the proletariat.

The ostensible mission of these groups was to “ally” with the poor peasants in order to evict the kulaks from the village and win over the middle peasants for the kolkhoz. In fact, these always vague terms now lost all meaning. What really occurred was the forcible subjection of the whole village to the Party: “kulak” came to mean simply any muzhik who resisted collectivization and therefore became an “enemy.” Party workers, with the aid of the more indigent peasants, summarily dispossessed these “kulaks” of their lands and livestock, and either cut them adrift in the countryside or, more often, packed them into freight cars for exile to the north; for former “kulaks” were not allowed to join the new kolkhoz. In the course of collectivization, according to Politburo figures, some five million to six million persons were “dekulakized.” The tactical principle in the campaign of 1930 was to take the peasants by surprise and divide the village before resistance could be organized, and so finish the whole job before spring sowing.

zh: 然而除此之外，并没有真正的作战计划。没有足够数量的拖拉机或联合收割机准备就绪。新集体农庄的形式甚至还没有由党加以规定。它应当是一个“TOZ”，即松散的生产者联合组织，成员只共用工具？还是应当是一个劳动组合（artel），土地合并、共同耕种？还是应当采取集体农庄“最高”也最社会主义的形式——公社，一切合并，成员共同生活？
en: Beyond this, however, there was no real plan of campaign. No adequate number of tractors or harvester-combines was ready. The form of the new kolkhozes had not even been specified by the Party. Should it be a “TOZ,” or loose association of producers, whose members only pooled their tools? Or should it be an artel in which lands would be pooled and cultivated in common? Or should it be the “highest” and most socialist form of kolkhoz, the commune, where everything was pooled and the members lived communally?

zh: 在集体化运动之前，大多数集体农庄只是TOZ。运动一开始，党的积极分子就瞄准劳动组合，甚至越过它瞄准公社，把奶牛、猪、鸡、农民的菜园，甚至家用器具都集体化。与此同时，村里的教堂被关闭，钟被取下，神父被赶走。农民俄国的古老生活方式被一击粉碎。不用说，这一行动已不再是一个“计划”。“计划”与“消灭富农”一样，现在只是党攻打传统俄国村庄时的战斗口号。
en: Before the collectivization drive most kolkhozes were mere TOZs. Once the drive began, Party activists aimed for the artel, and even beyond it for the commune, collectivizing cows, pigs, chickens, the peasants’ garden plots, and even household implements. At the same time, the village church was closed, its bell taken down, and the priest chased off. The immemorial way of life of peasant Russia was shattered with one blow. Needless to say, this operation was no longer a Plan. “Plan,” along with “liquidation of the kulak,” was now only a battle cry in the Party’s storming of the traditional Russian village.

zh: 事情就这样进行了八个星期，随后宣布俄国农业已有55%集体化。实际上，一半的集体组织只存在于纸面上，其余大多数结构薄弱、缺乏设备。而且，农民的反抗完全出乎当局意料，他们开始用他们仅剩的手段进行抵抗：毁坏自己的财产，以免把它交给集体农庄。四百万匹马被宰杀，一千四百万头牛被杀吃掉。国家的拖拉机远远不足以替代失去的马匹，受过训练能操作那点少得可怜的机器的农民也远远不够。领导层开始意识到，需要为农村制定更周全的计划，以免整个运动以政权的灾难告终。
en: So matters proceeded for eight weeks, at which time it was announced that 55 percent of Russian agriculture had been collectivized. In reality, half of the collectives existed only on paper, and most of the others were weakly structured and lacking in equipment. The peasants, moreover, quite unexpectedly began to resist through the only means left to them: destruction of their property in order to avoid surrendering it to the kolkhoz. Four million horses were slaughtered, and fourteen million head of cattle were killed and eaten. The state had far too few tractors to replace the lost horses, and there were far too few peasants trained to operate what little machinery did exist. It began to dawn on the leadership that more-adequate plans for the countryside were needed lest the whole drive end in disaster for the regime.

zh: 因此，3月2日，斯大林被迫在一篇题为《胜利冲昏头脑》的著名文章中要求暂停。文章的要旨是：地方同志误解了党的指示，把集体化推得过了头，现在应当放慢速度。人们常把这篇文章作为斯大林虚伪的例证：既然是他本人怂恿了同志们，责任就在他。事实上，事情并不那么简单。斯大林及其手下确实鞭策党投入战斗，但队伍随后自行冲了出去，部分出于真正的热情，部分出于害怕如果不表现得足够积极就会被指控为“右倾”。因此地方积极分子常常对斯大林软下来感到愤怒。但这件事真正的罪魁祸首是党自身的风气——无论在下层还是领导层——这种风气是布尔什维克长期掌权期间形成的。
en: On March 2, therefore, Stalin was forced to call a temporary halt in a famous article entitled “Dizziness from Success.” Its burden was that the local comrades had misunderstood the Party’s directives, thus pushing collectivization to excessive lengths, and that they should now slow down. This article is usually cited as an example of Stalin’s hypocrisy: since he himself had egged the comrades on, the blame was his. In fact, matters are not so simple. Stalin and his men had indeed spurred the Party into battle, but the troops had then charged off on their own, in part out of genuine zeal and in part out of fear of being accused of “Rightism” if they were not adequately zealous. Thus local activists were often furious with Stalin for going soft. But the real culprit in this affair was the Party’s ethos itself, and in the ranks as much as in the leadership, as it had developed during the Bolsheviks’ long years in power.

zh: 然而斯大林的退却只是暂时的，仅仅持续整个播种季节。在接下来的三个月里，随着虚弱或纸面上的集体农庄被解散，加入集体农庄的农户比例降到23%。然后，1930年秋天，攻势以更有条理的方式恢复，政权开始摸索农村的新秩序。决定以劳动组合作为标准组织形式。此外，认为让单个农民保留自己的小屋、菜园和一些家畜是审慎的。机器这时开始到位，并集中在机器拖拉机站（MTS），每个站都设有一个政治部。党第一次在农村有了真正的据点。与此同时，农民现在没有役畜，没有机器拖拉机站就无法播种或收割，因此国家终于确保了它在收成中的份额。
en: Stalin’s retreat, however, was only temporary, merely for the duration of the sowing season. In the next three months the level of collectivization dropped to 23 percent of peasant households, as weak or paper kolkhozes were dissolved. Then in the fall of 1930 the offensive resumed more methodically, and the regime began to feel its way towards a new order in the countryside. It was decided that the artel would be the standard form of organization. In addition, it was deemed prudent to leave the individual peasant in possession of his hut, garden plot, and some domestic animals. Machinery now began to become available and was concentrated in Machine Tractor Stations, or MTSs, which were each given a political section. For the first time the Party had a genuine outpost in the countryside. At the same time, the peasants, now lacking draft animals, could neither sow nor reap without the MTS, and so the state was at last guaranteed its cut of the harvest.

zh: 这些措施促成了1931年的第二次集体化运动；到那年年底，加入集体农庄的农户比例升至52.7%，集体化的作物面积比例升至67.8%。但这是以一场同样凶猛、但比1930年更有控制的斗争为代价取得的。毁坏财产和屠宰役畜、牲畜的行为再次出现，这次规模比先前更大。总体而言，在集体化过程中，俄国牲畜数量减少约一半，某些种类减少得更多。随着旧村庄被拆解以组建新集体，近乎混乱的局面笼罩一切。与此同时，集体化和流放富农的一个主要副产品是古拉格的出现；在列宁时代它只是一项不大的事业，现在则成为苏联制度的一个主要组成部分——这一点后面再详述。
en: These measures produced a second collectivization drive in 1931; by the end of that year the percentage of peasant households in kolkhozes had increased to 52.7, and that of crop area collectivized to 67.8. But this was achieved only at the cost of an equally ferocious but more controlled struggle than the one in 1930. Destruction of property and the slaughter of draft animals and livestock resumed, this time on a greater scale than before. Altogether, in the course of collectivization Russia’s livestock population declined by about half, and in certain categories by even more. Near-chaos reigned as the old village was dismantled to form the new collective. At the same time, a major by-product of collectivization and the deportation of kulaks was the emergence of the Gulag; only a modest enterprise under Lenin, it now became a major component of the Soviet system—but of this more later.

zh: 第二次集体化运动很快导致饥荒，饥荒始于1932年秋收之后，一直持续到次年秋天。虽然1932年的收成略低于平均，但这不是饥荒的原因。原因在于农民继续抵抗政权的意图，以及政权为彻底摧毁农民抵抗意志而作出的回应。触发因素是1932年5月开放农民市场，采取这一措施是因为相信新的集体农庄制度已足够稳固，能满足国家需要。但粮食采购量骤降，党的控制被证明不足以补救。如同乌拉尔—西伯利亚方法的时代，斯大林认为农民在藏匿粮食，地方党的官员在夺取粮食时不够无情。于是党的压力急剧加大，要给农民一个深刻教训：国家径行拿走其采购定额，不管会剩下什么，即便当局很清楚这可能造成饥荒。因此，1932—1933年伏尔加河流域和乌克兰的饥荒被称为“恐怖饥荒”。
它夺去了六百万到一千一百万人的生命，视估算方法而定。尽管这是本世纪最重大的罪行之一，当时却在很大程度上对外部世界保密，甚至对苏联人口中未直接受影响的部分也保密。而饥荒奏效了。它终于为党在农村带来了胜利。农民再也不会有反抗苏维埃政权的意志。
en: The second collectivization drive soon resulted in famine, which began after the harvest of 1932 and continued until the following autumn. Although the 1932 harvest was somewhat smaller than average, this was not the famine’s cause. The cause, rather, was continuing peasant resistance to the regime’s purposes and the regime’s answering drive to break the peasants’ will to resist once and for all. The triggering circumstance was the opening of peasant markets in May 1932, a measure undertaken in the belief that the new kolkhoz system was sufficiently well established to supply the state’s needs. But grain procurements plummeted and Party controls proved inadequate to remedy matters. As in the days of the Urals-Siberian method, Stalin believed that the peasants were concealing food and that local party officials were not ruthless enough in taking it from them. So Party pressure was drastically increased to teach the peasants a great lesson: The state simply took its procurement quota without regard to what would be left over, even though the authorities well knew that famine could result. Thus the famine of 1932-1933 in the Volga valley and Ukraine has been called a “terror famine.”

It claimed from six, to eleven million lives, depending on how the estimate is made. Even though this was one of the greatest criminal acts of the century, at the time it was largely kept secret from the outside world and even from those parts of the Soviet population not directly affected. And the famine worked. It at last brought victory to the Party in the countryside. The peasants would never again have the will to defy Soviet power.
