zh: 于是，到1934年，71.4%的农户已集体化；到1936年，达到90%。俄国两千五百万个农户变成了二十四万个集体农庄。庄稼汉俄国那无数分散的自给自足的生产单位——政权在新经济政策下不得不与之周旋——现在被集中到一个更“合理”、也就是更易于管理的社会主义生产组织中。
en: Thus, by 1934, 71.4 percent of village households were collectivized, and by 1936, 90 percent. The 25 million peasant homesteads of Russia had become 240,000 kolkhozes. The myriad of dispersed subsistence units of muzhik Russia with which the regime had had to contend under the NEP was now concentrated into a more “rational,” that is manageable, socialist organization of production.

zh: 与此同时，与集体农庄制度并行，政权建立了一个规模较小的国营农场（sovkhoz）网络。这些大型机械化单位被设想为农业工厂，农民在其中作为工人劳动。虽然国营农场只占苏联农业的很小一部分，但它们被视为农村社会主义的理想形式，预示着未来著名的“城乡矛盾”终将得到解决。
en: At the same time, and parallel to the kolkhoz system, the regime created a less extensive network of sovkhozes, or state farms. These large mechanized units, in which the peasants labored as workers, were supposed to be agrarian factories. Although the sovkhozes accounted for only a modest proportion of Soviet agriculture, they were viewed as the ideal form of socialism in the countryside, an anticipation of the future in which the famous “contradiction between town and country” would at last be resolved.

zh: 然而，农村的物质改造不应被夸大。新制度稳定下来、其组织方式被1935年《集体农庄章程》法典化之后，丘特切夫笔下那座简陋的俄国村庄依然如故：未上漆的原木小屋歪向一边，一间房的商店，以及较近才有的只有一间房的学校。日常生活仍然如此传统，以致到1939年只有4.5%的集体农庄通了电。但与此同时，村里的食物比1929年甚至1913年要少得多。
en: Yet the material transformation of the countryside should not be exaggerated. After the new system had shaken down and its mode of organization was codified in the Kolkhoz Charter of 1935, the humble Russian village of Tiutchev was still very much there, with its unpainted log huts listing to one side, its one-room store, and its more recent one-room school. Daily life was still so traditional that by 1939 only 4.5 percent of kolkhozes had electricity. At the same time, however, there was much less to eat in the village than had been the case in 1929 or even in 1913.

zh: 村里改变的是其政治和经济组织。庄稼汉并没有像斯大林承诺的那样亲自坐在拖拉机上；拖拉机全都在为若干集体农庄服务的机器拖拉机站手里。因此，机器拖拉机站成了党控制农村的枢纽；而在集体化之前，农村从未真正受到党的有效控制。布尔什维克对俄国的征服——1921年尚未越出城市的大门——现在完成了，整个国家终于被占领。
en: What had changed in the village was its political and economic organization. The muzhik was not personally seated on a tractor, as Stalin had promised; the tractors were all in the hands of the MTS that serviced a number of kolkhozes. Thus the MTS had become the pivot of the Party’s presence in the countryside, which until collectivization had not known effective Party control. The Bolshevik conquest of Russia that had not gone beyond the gates of her cities in 1921 was now completed, and the whole country was at last occupied.

zh: 然而，政权被迫以农民自留地的形式向农民作出了一项重大让步。诚然，这项让步是勉强的；在其后整个历史中，苏维埃政权将不断设法缩小这些自留地的作用。但它从未成功消除它们，因此俄国将继续存在一小部分私营企业和一个边缘性市场。而且，这些农民自留地很快就会生产出该国不成比例的大量食物；例如1937年，约25%的食物来自仅5%的耕地。
en: Yet the regime had been forced to make one significant concession to the peasantry in the form of the individual peasant plot. To be sure, this concession was made grudgingly; during the remainder of its history the Soviet regime would constantly strive to decrease the role of these plots. But it would never succeed in eliminating them, and so a small measure of private enterprise and a marginal market would continue to exist in Russia. These peasant plots, moreover, would soon produce an inordinate proportion of the country’s food; in 1937. for example, around 25 percent of the food came from only 5 percent of the cultivated land.

zh: 然而，这些农民自留地无法挑战国家对主要作物——粮食——的控制；获得这种控制正是集体化的真正目的。1933年以后，国家有了稳定的粮食供应，而且不必为此付钱，因为它不再受市场约束去用消费品向农民提供任何有意义的补偿。于是，一个经济问题再次通过政治手段得到解决，
（administrirovanie）取代了市场。俄国市民社会唯一在革命后幸存下来的堡垒——农民——作为一支独立和自我管理的力量被消灭了。正是这个阶级的暴动使一小撮狂热分子得以在1917年夺取政权；现在，它成了这些狂热分子的主要受害者。
en: Nonetheless, these peasant plots could not challenge the state’s control over the main crop, grain; obtaining that control had been the real purpose of collectivization. After 1933 the state had a stable supply of food for which it did not have to pay, since it was no longer constrained by the market to offer the peasants any significant compensation in consumer goods. Thus once again an economic problem had been solved by political means, and

had replaced the market, The only bastion of Russian civil society that had survived the Revolution, the peasantry, was eliminated as an independent and self-managing force. The class whose jacquerie alone had permitted a small band of fanatics to seize power in 1917 now became the chief victim of their fanaticism.

zh: 传统俄国村庄就这样被一劳永逸地碾碎。更准确地说，在1861年解放不到一个世纪之后，农民又被党国重新农奴化了。党现在可以着手建设社会主义的核心事业：突击工业化。
en: Thus the traditional Russian village was crushed once and for all. To be more exact, less than a century after their Emancipation in 1861, the peasants were reenserfed by the Party-state. The Party now could get on with the central business in the building of socialism: crash industrialization.

zh: 然而，斯大林的集体化对国家是一场彻头彻尾的灾难，而他的工业化运动——尽管代价巨大、残酷和浪费——却是一项重大的历史成就。它确实是苏联实验唯一真正的成就。
en: Yet, whereas Stalin’s collectivization was an unrelieved disaster for the country, his industrialization drive—for all its inordinate cost, brutality, and wastefulness—was a significant historical accomplishment. It was indeed the Soviet experiment’s only real achievement.

zh: 它使大部分城市人口产生真正的自豪感；它是该政权另一项主要成就——第二次世界大战胜利——的重要因素；它赋予这个国家一副最起码的现代骨架，不可逆转地把农民俄国变成城市社会，或者至少是城市社会的仿影。最后，它是布尔什维克唯意志主义的至高壮举。
en: It was a source of genuine pride for much of the urban population; it was a major factor in the regime’s other main achievement, its victory in the Second World War; it endowed the country with a bare-bones modernity that irreversibly transformed peasant Russia into an urban society, or at least the simulacrum of an urban society. And, finally, it was the supreme feat of Bolshevik voluntarism.

zh: 这场跃入技术社会水晶宫的大跃进，在很大程度上是党对农民俄国开战的产物。因为1929年后工业化冲刺被集体化运动所加速，正如集体化运动是由工业化冲刺所催生。两个过程相互滋养、同步演进（
），尽管并非以计划所预期的方式。计划预见到的是通过共同富裕实现相互支持；而两条“战线”之间的实际联系，是通过互相引发恐慌，继而互相助长狂热。
en: This great leap into the Crystal Palace of technological society was very much the product of the Party’s war against peasant Russia. For the rush to industrialization after 1929 was accelerated by the drive to collectivize, just as the drive to collectivize had been generated by the rush to industrialize. The two processes fed on each other and evolved

, though not in the way the Plan had anticipated. The Plan had foreseen mutual support through mutual enrichment; the interconnection between the two “fronts” was in fact through reciprocal panic leading to reciprocal intoxication.

zh: 具体而言，1929年底一旦作出全面集体化的决定，就认为必须加速计划以实现集体农庄的机械化。因此，12月1日，最佳计划的目标被向上“修订”。几天后，一次“突击队”代表大会号召在四年内完成五年计划，这立即成为政府政策（计划现在正式于1932年12月31日结束）。事实上，原初技术官僚版本的计划——它已经足够乌托邦——被抛弃了。“计划”转而意味着工业中一系列突击优先事项，或选定的战略目标，无论代价如何都要实现。同样，计划成为对党和民众进行心理动员的工具，一种让部队在“工业战线”上继续前进的机制。但除此之外，工业战线上的作战部署并不比同时开辟的农业战线更精确；工厂和铸造厂最初的局面几乎与农村一样灾难性。
en: Concretely, once the decision for full collectivization was taken in late 1929, it was considered necessary to accelerate the Plan in order to mechanize the kolkhozes. Accordingly, on December I the targets of the optimal Plan were “amended” upward. A few days later a congress of “shock brigades” called for completing the Five-Year Plan in four years, and this immediately became government policy (the Plan would now officially end on December 31, 1932). In fact, the Plan in its original technocratic version, which was already utopian enough, was discarded. “Plan” came to mean instead a series of crash priorities, or selected strategic objectives, in industry, to be achieved whatever the cost. By the same token, the Plan became a device for the psychological mobilization of the Party and the population, a mechanism to keep the troops advancing on the “industrial front.” But beyond this there was no more of a precise order of battle on the industrial front than on the simultaneously opened agricultural front, and the initial results in the factories and foundries were almost as disastrous as those in the countryside.

zh: 进攻的口号是“技术决定一切”，意思是只要获得工业机器，就会自动带来现代效率和社会主义成功。这种简单化的做法不仅是斯大林对马克思主义理解粗浅的结果；它非常符合马克思本人身上突出的技术决定论倾向——例如这位创始人宣称，手磨产生封建领主的社会，蒸汽磨产生工业资本家的社会；这一观点在列宁的论断“社会主义等于苏维埃政权加电气化”中得到延续。斯大林只是实际上宣布“高炉产生社会主义社会”，更新了这个等式。除了这一马克思主义传统，还必须加上美国作为现代性典范的例子；这种形象因第一次世界大战而在整个欧洲出现，并被泰勒制的劳动效率公式放大，后来又由福特制的流水线奇迹所放大。而事实上，第一个五年计划的技术，就是几年前先进美国的技术。于是，在俄国建设马克思主义社会主义，变得等同于一场“赶上并超过美国”的竞赛。
en: The slogan of the attack was “technology decides everything,” by which was meant that the mere acquisition of industrial machinery would automatically yield modern efficiency and socialist success. This simplistic approach was not just the result of Stalin’s primitive understanding of Marxism; it was very much in the vein of a technological determinism prominent in Marx himself—as when the founder declared that the hand mill produces a society of feudal lords and the steam mill a society of industrial capitalists, a viewpoint continued in Lenin’s dictum that “socialism equals Soviet power plus electrification.” Stalin simply updated this equation by decreeing, in effect, that the blast furnace produces a socialist society. To this Marxist tradition must be added the example of America as the very model of modernity, an image that had emerged throughout Europe as a result of the First World War and that was amplified by the formulae for labor efficiency of Taylorism and later by the assembly line prodigies of Fordism. And in fact the technology of the First Five-Year Plan was that of advanced America only a few years earlier. Thus, building Marxist socialism in Russia came to be tantamount to a race “to catch up with and overtake America.”

zh: 因此，党把发展重工业或资本品工业作为其主要战略目标，并把所有资源投入将进一步促进工业化的项目。这就是计划现在全部的内容，因为党作出这一选择时，根本没有考虑其基本突击纲领将如何与轻工业、预算、劳动力或消费人口相关联。结果是1930年至1933年的一场“计划狂欢”
，在接连不断的危机中踉跄前行，几乎以崩溃告终。
en: The Party therefore took as its chief strategic objective the development of heavy or capital goods industry, and it threw all of its resources into projects that would promote still further industrialization. This was all that the Plan now amounted to, for the Party made this choice without giving any thought to how its basic crash programs would relate to light industry, to the budget, to the workforce, or to the consumer population. The result was a “bacchanalia of planning”
from 1930 to 1933 that reeled from crisis to crisis and almost ended in collapse.

zh: 这一努力的中心是重冶金。因此，攻势的主要优先事项是煤、铁和钢，以及机床和制造涡轮机、拖拉机、卡车和汽车的新工厂。

为配合这一努力，官僚机构也扩张了：最高国民经济委员会开始分化为各专业工业人民委员部（即部）。第一个是政治局委员奥尔忠尼启则领导的重工业人民委员部；他主要充当政治问题解决者，把技术管理留给更有资格的副手皮亚塔科夫。计划中最大的单一项目是乌拉尔—库兹巴斯联合企业，它把乌拉尔新城市马格尼托哥尔斯克的铁与一千英里外中国边境附近的库兹涅茨克煤田连接起来。这个项目使苏联有了一个替代革命前乌克兰的克里沃罗格—顿巴斯煤钢联合企业的选择；后者已不够现代，而且太靠近西部边境，容易受到攻击。
en: At the center of this effort was heavy metallurgy. The Offensive’s chief priorities therefore were coal, iron, and steel, together with machine tools and new factories to turn out turbines, tractors, trucks, and automobiles.

To accommodate this effort, the bureaucracy expanded, too: Vesenkha began to diversify into specialized industrial People’s Commissariats, or ministries. The first of these was that of Heavy Industry under Politburo member Ordzhonikidze, who functioned largely as political trouble-shooter, leaving technical management to his better-qualified deputy. Piatakov. The greatest single project of the Plan was the Urals-Kuzbas Combine, which linked the iron of the new Urals city of Magnitogorsk with the Kuznetsk coal basin one thousand miles away on the Chinese frontier. This project gave the Soviet Union an alternative to the pre-Revolutionary Krivoi Rog-Donbas coal-steel combine in Ukraine, which was no longer modern enough and was too vulnerably close to the western frontier.

zh: 其他高度优先的项目包括斯大林格勒拖拉机厂，后来还有下诺夫哥罗德（很快改名为高尔基）的莫洛托夫汽车厂，以及莫斯科的卡冈诺维奇地铁。与此同时，电气化受到高度重视，第聂伯水电站大坝即为代表（这也是胡佛水坝和田纳西流域管理局的时代）。交通运输受重视程度较低：该部门的主要项目包括横贯中亚的土耳其斯坦—西伯利亚铁路，以及波罗的海—白海运河；后者由囚犯劳工修建，由于是用手铲挖掘的，结果太浅而无法使用。
en: Other high-priority projects were the Stalingrad Tractor Factory, or later the Molotov Automobile Works in Nizhnii-Novgorod (soon renamed Gorky), and the Kaganovich Metro in Moscow. At the same time, a major emphasis was placed on electrification, as exemplified by the great Dnieprostroi Dam (this was also the era of the Hoover Dam and the Tennessee Valley Authority). A lesser emphasis was placed on transportation: major projects in this sector included the Turksib Railroad across Central Asia and the Baltic-White Sea Canal, which was built with convict labor and turned out to be too shallow for use because it had been dug with hand shovels.

children: 〔译注〕白海—波罗的海运河于1933年开放通航；水深不足会限制某些船只，但并非完全不能通行。
〔译注〕白海—波罗的海运河于1933年开放通航；水深不足会限制某些船只，但并非完全不能通行。

zh: 为资助这一工业化纲领，政权把粮食卖到国外，甚至在饥荒期间也是如此。这使它能够进口西方设备，并雇用西方工程师来建造马格尼托哥尔斯克和其他试点项目。以这些项目为基础，政权随后利用自己的资源在全国各地建厂，生产所需的汽车、拖拉机和其他重型设备。即便如此，在整个三十年代，政权仍严重依赖外国样板：例如它的ZIS-ZIL高级轿车实质上是一辆苏联别克；斯大林格勒拖拉机厂是卡特彼勒拖拉机厂的一模一样的复制品；高尔基汽车厂则是福特工厂的复制。
但模仿虽然是一条快速成长之路，却有其代价：苏联工业虽然很快就能生产大量工业品，却很少能达到具有国际竞争力的质量，而且几乎从未发明新产品或新技术。
en: To finance this industrialization program, the regime sold grain abroad, even during the famine. This allowed it to import Western equipment and to hire Western engineers to build Magnitogorsk and other pilot projects. With these projects as a base, the regime then used its own resources to build factories across the country to produce the automobiles, tractors, and other heavy equipment it needed. Even so, throughout the thirties the regime remained heavily dependent on foreign models: Its ZIS-ZIL limousine, for example, was essentially a Soviet Buick; the Stalingrad tractor factory was a literal copy of the Caterpillar tractor factory; and the Gorky automobile works was the copy of a Ford plant.

But imitation, though a quick road to growth, had its costs: Soviet industry, although it was soon able to produce great quantities of industrial goods, was rarely able to achieve internationally competitive quality, and it almost never invented new products or technologies.

zh: 此外，所有这些建设都是在接连不断的、近乎混乱的危机中进行的。第一次危机发生在1930年夏。轻工业或消费品工业被剥夺了投资资本，开始萎缩，而与此同时，随着被“去富农化”的农民和其他新工人涌入城市，劳动力规模膨胀。突然之间，消费品、食品、住房和城市交通都匮乏，无法满足工人最基本的需求。物价飞涨，政权不得不诉诸近乎全民的配给制，以照料迅速膨胀的城市人口。由于随着计划推进，生活条件只是一天天恶化，“1933年[俄国]是有记录以来和平时期最急剧的生活水平下降达到顶点的一年。”
但话说回来，俄国当时并不是真正的和平时期。
en: Moreover, all of this construction was carried out amidst constant crisis bordering on chaos. The first crisis occurred in the, summer of 1930. The light or consumer-goods industry, deprived of investment capital, began to sag just as the labor force swelled in size with the influx of “dekulakized” peasants and other new workers into the cities. There was suddenly a dearth of consumer goods, food, housing, and urban transportation to meet the most elementary needs of the workers. Prices soared and the regime was obliged to resort to near-universal rationing to care for the burgeoning urban population. Because conditions only grew worse as the Plan progressed, “1933 [in Russia] was the culmination of the most precipitous peacetime decline in living standards known in recorded history.”
But then it was not really peacetime in Russia.

zh: 到1930年秋，随着消费品消失、物价上涨，情况已很清楚：与预期相反，工业生产总体上正在下降。
由于这紧接在集体化第一次惨败之后发生，党内开始有人要求放慢工业化的“速度”。然而，斯大林在城市问题上同样不肯退让。他的回应既包括坚决拒绝降低现有速度，也包括努力应对因劳动力素质不足而造成的新危机。
因为此时已经很明显，技术不会决定一切，国家花大代价买来的新机器，没有能干的工人就无法运转。
en: By the fall of 1930, as consumer goods disappeared and as prices rose, it became clear that, contrary to expectations, industrial production overall was falling.

Since this occurred in the immediate wake of the first fiasco of collectivization, voices within the Party began to call for a slowing of the “tempos” of industrialization. Yet Stalin was no more to be turned back in the city than he had been in the village. His response combined an adamant refusal to reduce existing tempos with an effort to cope with an emerging new crisis caused by the inadequacies of the labor force.
For it had by now become apparent that technology would not decide everything, and that the country’s dearly-bought new machinery would not work without competent workers.

zh: 在1931年7月的一次讲话中，斯大林试图让政权的目的迁就“人的因素”的脆弱。这样做时，他制定了一项妥协政策，类似于他同时向农民让步、允许农民保留自留地。迄今为止，布尔什维克的工资政策是平均主义的；斯大林现在谴责“平均化”（
）是不符合马克思主义的、“小资产阶级的”。他宣称，真正的社会主义政策是给工人计件工资，即按他们生产的商品数量付酬。换句话说，面对一种未曾预料、几乎普遍的匮乏，斯大林诉诸不平等报酬来刺激生产。这是他的胡萝卜。
en: In a speech he delivered in July 1931, Stalin sought to accommodate the purposes of the regime to the frailty of the “human factor.” In doing so, he produced a compromise policy that was analogous to his simultaneous concession of individual plots to the peasants. Hitherto, Bolshevik wage policy had been egalitarian; Stalin now denounced “levelling” (

) as un-Marxist and “petty-bourgeois.” The true socialist policy, he declared, was to offer workers piece-rates, or payment in accordance with the quantity of goods they produced. In other words, faced with a situation of unanticipated and almost universal scarcity, Stalin resorted to unequal rewards to stimulate production. This was his carrot.

zh: 斯大林同时挥出了他的大棒，攻击“劳动力流动”，即劳动力在普遍匮乏的新世界里寻找改善机会的游牧习惯。因此，实行了国内护照制度：每个人必须在警察局登记才能在某个城市居住；住房和口粮的获得与固定就业挂钩；对旷工实行刑事处罚。这是一个进程的开端，到那个十年结束时，它将恢复十九世纪警察控制手段的劳动手册，乃至以送入古拉格相威胁，把工人束缚在工作岗位上。尽管这套制度不如集体农庄的新农奴制严厉——在那里农民根本没有护照——但它同样把人口从属于政权的目的。
en: Stalin unveiled his stick when he also attacked the “fluidity of labor,” or the nomadic habits of a labor force searching for some improvement in the new world of endemic scarcity. Accordingly, internal passports were introduced: each person had to be registered with the police in order to live in any given city; access to housing and rations was linked to fixed employment; and criminal penalties were introduced for absenteeism. This was the beginning of a process that by the end of the decade would bring back the nineteenth-century police device of labor books, and indeed the possibility of the Gulag, to tie workers to their jobs. Although this regimen was less severe than the neoserfdom of the kolkhoz—where peasants had no passports at all—it represented an analogous subordination of the population to the purposes of the regime.

zh: 但斯大林也着眼于未来，他力陈有必要创造一支堪称新工人阶级的队伍。
现有劳动力，尤其是最近迁入城市的农民，缺乏这种新工业秩序所需的“文化”；而拥有这种“文化”的资产阶级专家在政治上不可靠——就像内战期间红军的沙皇军官。工业攻势开始时，又发生了两场“破坏分子”公审：1930年对所谓“工业党”的“资产阶级”工程师的审判，以及1931年对孟什维克（即早期计划人员）的审判。
但对熟练人员的需求被证明如此之大，以致作为权宜之计，斯大林现在叫停了这种“针对专家的迫害”（spets-baiting）。至于长期解决办法，他在“文化”战线上发动了一场大规模攻势，号召开展技术教育，以培养社会主义的“工人知识分子”。与此同时，可靠的无产者要通过教育“被推上前去”担任管理职务；这一
（vydvizhenie）过程将使无产阶级专政拥有自己的“干部”队伍，即技术人员。正如内战结束时沙皇军官被逐步清出红军、由新培养的红色学员取代，在工业大军中，资产阶级军官团现在也要由新训练的红色管理者取代。
en: But Stalin also looked to the future when he urged the necessity of creating what would amount to a new working class.

The existing labor force, especially the recently transplanted peasants, lacked the requisite “culture” for this new industrial order; and the bourgeois specialists who had this “culture” were politically unreliable—like the tsarist officers of the Red Army during the Civil War. At the start of the industrial offensive there had been two new show trials of “wreckers,” that of the so-called Industrial Party of “bourgeois” engineers in 1930, and that of the Mensheviks (that is, the early planners) in 1931.

But the need for skilled personnel had proved to be so great that, as a stopgap solution, Stalin now called off this “spets-baiting.” As for a long-term solution, he launched a massive attack on the “cultural” front by calling for technological education that would produce a socialist “worker intelligentsia.” Simultaneously, reliable proletarians were to be “moved forward” by means of education into managerial positions, a process of

that would give the dictatorship of the proletariat its own class of “cadres,” or technical personnel. Just as tsarist officers were phased out of the Red Army at the end of the Civil War in favor of newly educated Red Cadets, so in the industrial army the bourgeois officer corps was now to be replaced by newly trained Red managers.

zh: 1935年，这种对“人的因素”的强调达到顶点。在普通产业工人层面，突击工作和社会主义竞赛的原则现在被制度化到斯达汉诺夫运动中。

一位名叫斯达汉诺夫的煤矿工人，在当局帮助下为自己创造了人为的理想工作条件，从而超额完成了既定的煤炭生产“定额”。他立即被塑造成英雄，各行各业的工人被激励去效仿他的壮举。这类壮举之所以可能，是因为当时俄国生产率如此之低，迅速提高它是可行的；它们之所以可能，还因为相当多的工人确实被建设社会主义工业的热情所感动。但一旦这些微型跃进出现，它们就成为所有工人的新定额；因此，无产阶级群众比斯达汉诺夫运动之前受到更厉害的“压榨”。不过，计件的“社会主义劳动英雄”确实在建成后的斯大林主义制度中成为某种工人贵族。
en: In 1935 this emphasis on the “human factor” reached its culmination. At the level of the industrial rank and file, the principles of shock work and socialist emulation were now institutionalized in the Stakhanovite movement.

A coal miner named Stakhanov, with the aid of the authorities, created for himself artificially ideal conditions of work and thereby overfulfilled the established “norm” for coal production. He was immediately made a hero, and workers in all fields were spurred to emulate his feat. Such feats were possible because Russian productivity at the time was so low that it was feasible to raise it very quickly; they were possible also because a significant number of workers were genuinely moved by zeal for the building of socialist industry. But once these mini-leaps forward had been made, they furnished the new norms for all workers; the proletarian mass was thus “sweated” more than it had been before the Stakhanovite movement. Still, piece-rate “heroes of socialist labor” did become a kind of worker-aristocracy in the completed Stalinist system.

zh: 但斯大林对工业军官团更加关怀，因为他们的技能对制度的成功最为关键。因此，1931年以后，政权扶持精英高等教育，但只面向人口中有前途的分子；这些“干部”接受教育之后，就获得与其管理职责相称的物质和社会特权。
en: But Stalin was even more solicitous for the industrial officer corps, since its skills were the most essential of all for the system’s success. Accordingly, the regime after 1931 fostered elite higher education, but only for promising elements of the population; once educated, these “cadres” received material and social privileges commensurate with their managerial responsibilities.

zh: 然而，这些职责是根据各级党委控制的干部职务名称表（
）来分配的；因此，新干部最终被统称为“名录干部”。按干部职务名称表任命，在二十年代已作为一种行政手段出现，但只有在斯大林的工业化创造出大量新职位之后，这一制度才能产生一个真正的种姓。于是到1935年，这个群体已成为新社会秩序的顶点。因此，斯大林修订了总路线，宣称“最宝贵的资本是人”，而当时的新口号变成了“干部决定一切”。
en: These responsibilities, however, were assigned according to lists of posts (
) controlled by Party committees at various levels; the new cadres, therefore, eventually came to be known collectively as “the
.” Assignment by

list had emerged as an administrative device in the twenties, but it was only after Stalin’s industrialization had created a mass of new posts that this system could give rise to a veritable caste. Thus by 1935 this group had become the apex of the new social order. Stalin therefore revised the General Line by declaring that the most “precious capital of all is man,” and the new slogan of the day became “cadres decide everything.”

zh: 对其他领域中原初攻势目标的类似修订也发生了。1930年，随着国家从新经济政策的半市场经济转向通过计划分配资源，货币的地位再次受到质疑，就像战时共产主义时期一样。人们普遍认为——甚至斯大林本人也这样认为——货币将让位于企业之间的社会主义“产品交换”。然而，很快就明显看出货币无法废除，因为产品交换（实际上只是物物交换）对于正在形成的极大规模工业网络来说太笨重、太粗糙。于是，为了把货币这一异己力量套上计划的缰绳，政府将所有信贷集中于国家银行。但工业增长如此混乱，计划者最终只好通过印钞机来为其融资。这与普遍匮乏相结合，在计划时期造成了六倍的通货膨胀。通货膨胀加剧了预测和协调的困难，使任何有实际意义的计划更加不可能。与此同时，由于工业工资跟不上通货膨胀，也由于农民几乎得不到报酬，卢布贬值成为另一种把财富从民众手中抽走、投入工业扩张的手段。
en: A similar revision of the original aims of the Offensive occurred in other areas as well. In 1930, as the country moved from the semi-market economy of the NEP to the allocation of resources through the Plan, the status of money once again came under question, as it had during War Communism. It was widely assumed, even by Stalin himself, that money would give way to socialist “product-exchange” between enterprises. However, it soon became apparent that money could not be abolished because product-exchange (which is in fact only barter) was too cumbersome and crude for what was becoming a very large-scale industrial network. And so to harness the alien force of money to the Plan, the government centralized all credit in the State Bank. But industrial growth was so chaotic that the planners ultimately took to financing it through the printing press. And this, in conjunction with universal scarcity, produced a sixfold increase in inflation during the period of the Plan. Inflation made planning in any meaningful sense still less possible by aggravating the difficulties of prediction and coordination. At the same time, because industrial wages did not keep up with inflation, and because the peasants were hardly paid at all, the falling value of the ruble became another means of siphoning wealth out of the population and into industrial expansion.

zh: 其结果是一种新变体的社会主义经济。市场被压制，代之以政治性的资源分配。但由于货币和价格被保留下来——不像战时共产主义结束时那样——它们获得了新的功能：把政权的政治目的传递给所有经济行为者。因此货币继续被使用，但方式与新经济政策时期大不相同。价格和工资不受供求支配；它们由国家规定。与此同时，对一切产品在其生产的每个阶段征收周转税，从而在需要的地方推高价格，而在需要的地方用补贴压低价格。这并没有在任何通常意义上平衡供求，但确实创造了一种为国家目的所必需的均衡。于是，价格、工资和税收都被要求服从政治逻辑，而非经济逻辑。
en: The result was a new variant of a socialist economy. The market was suppressed in favor of the political allocation of resources. But since money and prices were preserved, unlike at the end of War Communism, they acquired a new function, which was to transmit the political purposes of the regime to all economic actors. Thus money continued to be used, but in a fashion very- different from that during the NEP. Prices and wages were not governed by supply and demand; they were set by the state. At the same time, a turnover tax was levied on all products at each stage in their production, thereby driving prices up where desired, while subsidies were used to bring prices down where desired. This did not balance supply and demand in any usual sense, but it did create a kind of equilibrium that was necessary for state purposes. Thus prices, wages, and taxes were all made to obey a political, not an economic, logic.

zh: 于是出现了一种组织生产和分配的新公式，即一种无市场的货币经济。这一公式与最初的战时共产主义并不相同。在战时共产主义下，经济是官僚集中制的（至少在纸面上如此），但没有计划，也几乎没有货币。在斯大林主义制度中，有计划，也有货币。这个新制度显然无法与世界经济相衔接，因此卢布保持不可兑换，以把外部市场力量挡在外面。短期内，这种隔绝带来了加强国家对内部经济发展控制的优势。长期来看，它使苏联与外部发展的刺激相隔绝，从而成为该制度最终衰落的原因之一。
en: Thus there emerged a new formula for organizing production and distribution, that of a marketless money economy. This formula was not identical to that of the original War Communism. Under War Communism there was a bureaucratically centralized economy (at least on paper), but no Plan and virtually no money. In the Stalinist system there was a Plan and money. This new system obviously could not be meshed with the world economy, so the ruble remained nonconvertible in order to keep external market forces out. In the short run this insulation provided the advantage of enhancing state control over internal economic developments. In the long run it isolated the Soviet Union from the stimulus of external developments, and so turned out to be one of the causes of the system’s ultimate decline.

zh: 斯大林主义制度与最初的战时共产主义还有一个区别，这个区别也构成了新秩序中的一种反常。事实上，在计划之下，市场确实继续存在。首先是合法的集体农庄市场。其次是非法的黑市，即后来所谓的“影子经济”。这种也被称为“第二经济”的东西，规模很大，尽管具体未知。交换一部分用货币进行，一部分用政治恩惠支付。但无论支付形式如何，合法的计划经济离开这个黑暗的孪生兄弟就无法运转。工厂经理和普通消费者都需要它才能维持生计。把这些不可或缺的经济能量驱入地下、驱入非法状态，削弱了整个制度的肌理。这个因素最终也会侵蚀斯大林主义的命令经济。
en: There was still another difference between the Stalinist system and original War Communism, a difference that also constituted an anomaly in the new order. In fact, a market did continue to exist under planning. First, there was the legal kolkhoz market. Second, there was the illegal black market, or what later came to be known as the “shadow economy.” This “second economy,” as it was also called, was of large, if unknown, proportions. In part exchange was conducted with money, and in part goods were paid for by political favors. But regardless of the form of payment, the legal, planned economy could not function without this dark double. Both factory managers and ordinary consumers needed it just to survive. Driving these indispensable economic energies underground and into illegality weakened the whole fabric of the system. And this factor, too, would eventually erode the Stalinist command economy.

zh: 于是，在又一条战线上，布尔什维克即兴发挥，为一个未曾预料的问题找到了某种解决办法。而他们设计出的解决办法，再次以酝酿长期结构性灾难为代价，提供了短期优势。
en: Thus, on still another front the Bolsheviks had improvised their way into a solution of sorts to an unanticipated problem. And the solution they devised once again offered a short-term advantage at the cost of preparing a long-term structural disaster.

zh: 到1933年，斯大林的大跃进在农业、工业和财政组织方面已经完成。第二个、也更为现实——尽管很难说“科学”——的五年计划已经开始，国家在1934年至1936年间经历了三年的增长。因此，到三十年代中期，第二场革命的结果已经稳定下来，一个新苏维埃制度在新经济政策的废墟上出现。但这个制度的整体结构是什么？驱动它的动力又是什么？
en: By 1933 Stalin’s great leap forward had been completed in agriculture, industry, and the organization of finance. A second and more realistic—though hardly “scientific”—Five-Year Plan had begun, and the country knew three years of growth between 1934 and 1936. Thus by mid-decade the results of the Second Revolution had been stabilized, and a new Soviet system had emerged on the ruins of the NEP. But what was the overall structure of this system? And what was the dynamic driving it?

zh: 首先，政权实现了其优先经济目标。前面提到的所有重工业项目，甚至更多，都完成了；即便没有按计划完成，至少也是以极短的时间完成。此外，俄国经济的重心不可逆转地从农业转向工业，从乡村转向城市。三十年代期间，约三千万农民被迫离开家乡，迁往城市：这是历史上规模最大、速度最快的城市化飞跃。
en: First of all, the regime had achieved its priority economic objectives. All the heavy industrial projects mentioned earlier, and then some, were completed, if not according to plan, at least in very short order. Moreover, the balance of the Russian economy was irreversibly shifted from agriculture to industry, and from country to city. Some thirty million peasants were uprooted and transferred to the city in the course of the thirties: This was the largest and most rapid leap in urbanization in history.

zh: 如此大规模的农村人口外流，当然不能由俄国那些粗陋的新工业城市的吸引力来解释。相反，它是政权通过

（trudoden）制度——衡量并酬付集体农庄庄员劳动的制度——设计出来的。每个家庭被要求完成的工作单位故意只给极低的报酬，以致这些工作基本上由妇女、儿童和老人承担。这一制度显然是集体农业生产率低下的一个主要原因。但与此同时，它实际上迫使壮年男子离开土地去工业中工作，而在政权眼中，这正是它的道理所在。的确，这种经济强制常常辅以集体农庄与工厂之间签订的活人转让合同。而一旦进入新城市，这些前庄稼汉就被速成教育、“开化”，并灌输马克思列宁主义原则。
en: Such a massive rural exodus, of course, cannot be explained by the lure of Russia’s raw new industrial cities. Rather, it was engineered by the regime through the

, or labor-day, system of measuring and rewarding the work of kolkhozniki. The work units required from each household deliberately received such low remuneration that they would be supplied basically by women, children, and oldsters. This system obviously was a major cause of the low productivity of collective agriculture. At the same time, however, it virtually forced ablebodied men off the land to work in industry, and this was its rationale in the eyes of the regime. Indeed, this economic compulsion was often supplemented by contracts passed between kolkhozes and factories for the transfer of live souls. And once in the new cities, these ex-muzhiks were summarily educated, “cultivated,” and indoctrinated in the principles of Marxism-Leninism.

zh: 所有这些的经济结果是，到那个十年结束时，苏联拥有了一个“现代”工业经济，首次使俄国实现自给自足。该制度早先对外国样品、蓝图和专家的依赖已经结束；它现在完全用自己的资源生产全套基本工业设施和产品，从钢厂到机床到涡轮机，从煤到石油，从拖拉机到坦克，从汽车到飞机。这一成就使苏联与美国同属一个独特的类别：两者都比任何欧洲大国或日本自给自足得多。而对俄国来说，随着三十年代国际局势日益危险，这绝非小事。
en: The economic result of all of this was that by the end of the decade the Soviet Union had a “modern” industrial economy that for the first time made Russia autarkic. The system’s earlier dependence on foreign prototypes, blueprints, and experts had ended; it now produced the full panoply of basic industrial products, from steel mills to machine tools to turbines, from coal to oil, from tractors to tanks, and from automobiles to airplanes, entirely with its own resources. This achievement put the Soviet Union in a unique category with the United States: Both were much more self-sufficient than any European power or Japan. And for Russia this was no small matter as the international situation grew more perilous in the thirties.

zh: 的确，从一开始，国防就是工业化的一个动机，斯大林1931年那句名言即表明了这一点：俄国绝不能再允许自己被打败。但在工业化开始时，国防并不是主要动机；主要动机显然是给党现有的“上层建筑”垫上一个工业的、无产阶级的“基础”，从而使党能够在这个国家内作为建设社会主义的工具而存续。因此，在颠倒的苏维埃世界里，工业化的首要目的是使俄国现实符合马克思主义的社会学假设。
en: Indeed, from the beginning national defense had been one motive for industrialization, as was evident in Stalin’s famous remark in 1931 that Russia should never allow herself to be beaten again. But defense was not the primary motive at the outset of industrialization; that motive clearly was to put an industrial and proletarian “base” under the existing “superstructure” of the Party, and thereby to make the Party viable within the country as the vehicle for building socialism. Thus, in the inverted Soviet world, the first purpose of industrialization was to bring Russian reality into line with Marxist sociological postulates.

zh: 1929—1932年间，纳粹威胁并不存在，日本1931年占领满洲也很难说是对苏维埃俄国的重大威胁。对国际安全的持续关注也不是民族主义的表现；它毋宁意味着一种关切：保卫革命及其党国，抵御正在包围它的世界资本主义。最显著地体现这一点的是1927年那场想象出来的战争恐慌，以及斯大林1928年的声明：国际资本主义的稳定已经结束，苏联应当警惕英法帝国主义进攻这一完全不可能的威胁。因此，国际局势对苏维埃突击工业化的影响，不能归因于任何具体的、在当时切实存在的威胁，而应归因于苏维埃对“资本主义”世界由意识形态导致的偏执。
en: In 1929-1932 the Nazi threat did not exist, and Japan’s occupation of Manchuria in 1931 was hardly a major menace to Soviet Russia. Nor was the constant preoccupation with international security an expression of nationalism; it signified, rather, a concern to defend the Revolution and its Party-state against encircling world capitalism. This was revealed most notably by the imagined war scare of 1927 and by Stalin’s declaration in 1928 that the stabilization of international capitalism had ended and that the Soviet Union should be on guard against the totally improbable menace of an Anglo-French imperialistic assault. Thus, the influence of the international situation on the Soviets’ crash industrialization can be attributed not to any specific or, at the time, realistic threat, but to the Soviets’ ideologically induced paranoia about the “capitalist” world.

zh: 这种挥之不去的恐惧直到1936—1937年希特勒进入莱茵兰、日本进入中国本部时才有了实质内容。这些事态终于给了苏联工业机器一个比社会主义更实际的目的。因为苏联工业化在十年中期获得其确定公式时，基本上是这样的：与政权宣称的目标相反，它是一个生产体系的恰恰反面——不是为了创造丰裕以最终满足人民需要，而是一个普遍挤压人民的体系，用以生产资本品来创造工业实力，以便生产更多资本品来创造更进一步的工业实力，并最终生产军备。这就是驱动成熟苏维埃制度的动力。
en: This abiding fear was given substance only in 1936-1937 when Hitler entered the Rhineland and Japan entered China proper. These developments at last gave the Soviet industrial plant a telos more practical than socialism. For Soviet industrialization, when it acquired its definitive formula in the mid-decade, amounted basically to this: Contrary to the declared goals of the regime, it was the opposite of a system of production to create abundance for the eventual satisfaction of the needs of the population; it was a system of general squeeze of the population to produce capital goods for the creation of industrial power, in order to produce ever more capital goods with which to produce still further industrial might, and ultimately to produce armaments. This was the dynamic driving the mature Soviet system.

zh: 于是，最初旨在为多元化经济扩张创造基础的重工业集中，本身变成了目的。军事力量的生产终于给了这个制度真正的目的和最终目的，而政权的命令—行政结构毫不费力地服务于这一目的。从1937年开始，苏联工业的重点日益转向军事生产；这一重点将一直是该制度的基本特征，直到它在1980年代末崩溃。
en: Thus the concentration on heavy industry that had initially been intended to create a base for diversified economic expansion became an end in itself. The production of military power at last gave the system its true purpose and final cause, and the regime’s command-administrative structures effortlessly lent themselves to this purpose. Beginning in 1937 the emphasis of Soviet industry shifted increasingly to military production; this emphasis would remain basic to the system until its collapse in the late 1980s.

zh: 这些发展的一个伴随结果是斯大林的新社会，一个高度分层的社会。这一现实当然不能得到承认。新秩序在1936年被正式定为“社会主义”，并被说成是建立在三个非对抗性阶级——工人、农民和“知识分子”（即新管理者）——之上，三者合在一起构成“人民”。然而事实上，报酬和权力完全按照一个人对政权的有用性和政治忠诚来分配。而且，在实际可能的范围内，一切都是由自上而下的命令来运行的。
en: A concomitant of these developments was Stalin’s new, highly stratified society. This reality, of course, could not be acknowledged. The new order was officially designated “socialist” in 1936, and it was held to be founded on three nonantagonistic classes—the workers, the peasants, and the “intelligentsia” (that is, the new managers)—which, taken together, constituted “the people.” In fact, however, rewards and power were doled out strictly in accordance with one’s usefulness and political loyalty to the regime. And, insofar as it was humanly possible, everything was run by command from the top down.

zh: 斯大林本人喜欢用适合新工业俄国的意象，把他的制度比作“一台机器及其齿轮”。
但他更偏爱的意象是军事的，他尤其把党比作一支“军队”：
en: Stalin himself, using imagery appropriate to the new industrial Russia, liked to compare his system to a “machine and its cogs.”
But his preferred imagery was military, and he likened the Party in particular to an “army”:

children: 如果看它的领导阶层，大约有三千到四千名最高一级领导人，我愿称之为我们党的将军团。
If we have in mind its leading strata, there are about 3,000 to 4,000 first rank leaders whom I would call our Party’s corps of generals.

zh: 然后大约有三万到四万名中层领袖，他们是我们党的军官团。
en: Then there are about 30,000 to 40,000 middle rank leaders who are our Party’s corps of officers.

zh: 然后大约有十万到十五万名党的下级指挥人员，可以说，他们是我们党的士官。
en: Then there are about 100,000 to 150,000 of the lower rank Party command staff who are, so to speak, our Party’s non-commissioned officers.

zh: 但这种意象只是把列宁1917年的原则推进了一步：鲁登道夫的战争社会主义可以轻易转变为战时共产主义；同样，它也进一步发展了托洛茨基1920年“劳动军事化”的纲领。甚至新经济政策及其“制高点”，也延续了这种军事精神。
en: But this imagery only took one step further Lenin’s principle of 1917 that Ludendorff’s War Socialism could easily be turned into War Communism, just as it further developed Trotsky’s program of 1920 for the “militarization of labor.” Even the NEP, with its “commanding heights,” continued this military spirit.

zh: 因此，第二次世界大战后，成熟的斯大林制度被美国苏联学家称为“命令经济”，这是恰如其分的。这个标签是德语词
的翻译；该词由逃离纳粹统治的难民创造，用来指称希特勒的四年计划——而元首的这个想法，既来自苏联经验，也来自对他昔日指挥官、一度政治盟友鲁登道夫的记忆。
1980年代末，俄国反共产主义的民主反对派采用了美国苏联学家的术语，并把它与苏联旧有的强制委婉语
（administrirovanie）混融起来，得出“行政—命令制度”这一标签。因为这些民主派需要这样一个迂回说法来替代“极权主义”，直到随着该制度的崩溃，后者不再是个禁忌词。然而无论使用什么术语——在鲁登道夫和列宁的时代，经斯大林及其身后——苏维埃制度始终是一种军事化的政治经济，无论在其组织结构还是在其产品上。它在战时共产主义下就是这样开始的，在第二次社会主义攻势中也是这样一路冲杀走向胜利的。
en: Thus it is only appropriate that after the Second World War the mature Stalin system came to be called by American Sovietologists a “command economy.” This label is a translation of the German word

, a term coined by refugees from Nazism to designate Hitler’s Four-Year Plan—an idea the Führer derived as much from the Soviet experience as from the memory of his old commander and sometime political ally, Ludendorff.
In the late 1980s the Russian democratic opposition to Communism adopted the American Sovietologists’ term and conflated it with the old Soviet euphemism for coercion,

, to yield the label “administrative-command system.” For these democrats needed such a circumlocution as a stand-in for “totalitarianism” until the latter term ceased to be taboo with the collapse of the system. Yet whatever term was used—in Ludendorff's and Lenin’s time, through Stalin’s and beyond—the Soviet system was always a militarized political economy, both in its organizational structure and in its products. This is how it began under War Communism, and this is how it stormed through to victory in the Second Socialist Offensive.

zh: 若干中途评估
en: SOME MID-COURSE EVALUATIONS

zh: 但作为发展经济学的一项实践，或作为落后条件下现代化的试点项目，斯大林革命又如何呢？诚然，这个问题无法与当时的政治环境分开，尤其是无法与下述情况分开：1937年以后，希特勒的威胁日益把苏联的经济努力转向非生产性的军事目的。即便如此，事实仍然是：斯大林的俄国通过一场非同寻常的自力更生行动，成为一个主要工业强国，而这种工业实力帮助造就了她在第二次世界大战中幸存这一具有重大政治意义的结果。
en: But what of the Stalin revolution as an undertaking in development economics, or as a pilot project of modernization under conditions of backwardness? To be sure, the question cannot be disentangled from the political circumstances of the day, in particular from the circumstance that after 1937 the menace of Hitler increasingly deflected the Soviet economic effort towards unproductive military ends. Even so, the fact remains that Stalin’s Russia, through an extraordinary bootstrap operation, became a major industrial power, and this industrial might helped make possible the politically productive result of her survival in the Second World War.

zh: 因此，在当时，实际上直到1980年代，对斯大林主义制度经济表现这一问题的回答，都会是“确实非常好”的某种变体。毕竟，1930年代初是大萧条的年月，当时美国有一千一百万人失业，德国有六百万人失业，美国的国民生产总值（GNP）平均每年下降8%。当马格尼托哥尔斯克的高炉点火时，匹兹堡和鲁尔的高炉却在熄火。斯大林在建设社会主义，而希特勒的褐衫队（冲锋队）在建设法西斯主义。市场的无政府状态似乎正在摧毁西方，而计划的理性正在东方创造一个崭新的世界。
en: Thus, at the time, and indeed until the 1980s, the answer to the question of the Stalinist system’s economic performance would have been one or another variant of “very good indeed.” The early 1930s, after all, were the years of the Great Depression, when eleven million were unemployed in the United States and six million in Germany, and when America’s gross national product (GNP) averaged an annual decline of 8 percent. While the blast furnaces of Magnitogorsk were being fired up, those of Pittsburgh and the Ruhr were being dampened down. Stalin was building socialism while Hitler’s Brown Shirts and Storm Troopers were building fascism. The anarchy of the market seemed to be destroying the West, while the rationality of the Plan was creating a new world in the East.

zh: 在整个战争和战后重建时期，这继续是西方许多人的视角。战争不仅把民主派和共产党人组成的人民阵线联盟聚集起来对抗法西斯主义，而且苏联的工业计划似乎解释了战时胜利，并使任何针对东欧重建的马歇尔计划都显得多余。于是，在从大萧条延伸到战后重建的漫长创伤中，西方自由主义意识中大致形成了一种对应关系：一边是不受管制的资本主义、经济危机和战争，另一边是计划、增长与和平——这对孪生星座在1914年前夜已初现端倪。
en: This continued to be the perspective of many in the West throughout the war and the period of postwar reconstruction. Not only did the war bring together a Popular Front coalition of democrats and Communists against fascism, but Soviet industrial planning seemed to explain the wartime victory and to make superfluous any Marshall Plan for Eastern Europe’s reconstruction. Thus, during the long trauma that extended from the Great Depression through the postwar reconstruction, a rough correlation emerged in the Western liberal consciousness between unregulated capitalism, economic crisis, and war on one hand, and planning, growth, and peace on the other—twin constellations already adumbrated on the eve of 1914.

zh: 这种心态的一个典型表现是奥地利经济学家卡尔·波兰尼的《大转型》。该书出版于1944年，谴责市场是“不自然的”，是现代世界弊病的主要根源。战后紧接着，社会主义者就在英国掌权，法国启动了自己形式的“指示性”计划；此后不久，西德将其经济奇迹描述为“社会市场经济”。在这种背景下，苏联的表现很容易赢得尊重，在许多圈子里还赢得宽容。
en: A prime expression of this mentality was

, by the Austrian economist Karl Polanyi. Published in 1944, this work condemned the market as “unnatural” and as the chief source of the modern world’s ills. Immediately after the war, socialists came to power in Britain, and France initiated her own form of “indicative” planning; shortly thereafter West Germany was to describe its economic miracle as a “social market.” Against this background the Soviet performance could easily earn respect and, in many quarters, indulgence.

zh: 三十年代，苏联公布的整个经济年增长数字约为16%到20%，这将使其表现成为当时世界上最好的。当时，西方的计算方法不够精细，西方经济学家对俄国也不够感兴趣，因此没有认真努力去核实苏联的表现。但新闻报导的共识——学术苏联学的前身——是俄国无疑取得了独一无二的惊人成就。战后，当学术苏联学家开始用西方科学方式计算国民生产总值时，他们得出1929—1940年间工业年增长率为12%到14%（尽管对农业和人均收入的计算数字要低得多）。一项对斯大林总体经济表现进行重新计算的重要研究认为，1955年的总产出是1928年的3.5倍；这换算为4.7%到6.7%的年均增长率（当然，仅三十年代的平均值还要更高，因为战争拉低了整体百分比）。
尽管所有这些计算都低于苏联官方数字，它们加在一起仍然构成历史上最伟大的经济表现之一，而这些计算将在接下来四十年里被无数教科书和新闻报道重复。
en: In the thirties the Soviets gave out per annum growth figures for the whole economy of some 16 percent to 20 percent, which would make their performance the best in the world until then. At the time, Western methods of calculation were not sufficiently refined, and Western economists were not sufficiently interested in Russia, to produce serious efforts at verifying the Soviet performance. But the consensus of journalistic reporting—the predecessor of academic Sovietology—was that Russia must surely be credited with uniquely spectacular achievements. And after the war, when academic Sovietologists began calculating the GNP in the Western scientific manner, they came up with annual growth rates for industry of 12 percent to 14 percent for the period 1929-1940 (though much lower figures were calculated for agriculture and per capita income). The major effort at recalculating Stalin’s overall economic performance held that total output, in 1955 was 3.5 times that of 1928; this translated into an average annual growth rate of between 4.7 percent and 6.7 percent (the average for the thirties alone, of course, was even higher because the war lowered the overall percentage).

Although all of these calculations were lower than the official figures given by the Soviets, they still added up to one of the great economic performances in history, and these calculations would be repeated in countless textbooks and journalistic accounts during the next four decades.

zh: 然后，在
（perestroika）期间，俄国经济学家带着对可追溯至1930年代的苏联统计数据的毁灭性批判加入了辩论。结果，1928—1940年苏联国民收入年均增长率，在内部人士尼古拉·什梅廖夫的估算中缩水到3.4%，在外部人士的估算中则不超过5%。
与此同时，西方专家大多沉默下来；共产主义垮台后，多数人能给出的唯一回答是：苏联数据缺陷如此之大，概念化任务如此艰巨，根本不可能确定1930年代的真实增长率。的确，一部重要的苏联经济史对整部苏联历史完全没有给出增长数字。于是我们又回到三十年代新闻界的评估：斯大林治下的苏联工业增长确实非常好。
en: Then, during

, Russian economists entered the debate with a devastating critique of Soviet statistics dating back to the 1930s. As a result, the average rate of growth of Soviet national income for the years 1928-1940 shrank to 3.4 percent in the estimate of the insider Nikolai Shmelev, or to no more than 5 percent in the estimates of outsiders.

At the same time, Western specialists largely fell silent; the only answer most would give after Communism’s fall was that Soviet data were so defective, and the task of conceptualization so daunting, that it is simply not possible to determine the true rate of growth in the 1930s. Indeed, the leading economic history of the USSR gives no growth figures at all for the whole of the Soviet story. So we are back with the journalistic assessment of the thirties that Soviet industrial growth under Stalin was very good indeed.

zh: 确实，我们不知道用经典国民生产总值术语衡量的苏联表现的确切数字。但从这个制度终结的方式，我们对其总体轮廓有相当不错的了解。对早先夸大数字的批判已经表明，苏联经济增长从未达到世界历史性的量级。维特在1890年代用温和得多的市场方法实现了工业年增长8%，其表现大概与斯大林相当。而明治日本整个经济年增长6%，做得更好；更不用说战后日本整个经济16%到18%的世界纪录——甚至邓小平的中国在1980年代的10%到12%。
en: It is true that we do not know the exact measurements of the Soviet performance in classic GNP terms. But we do have a pretty good idea of its general contours from the way the system ended. The critique of earlier, inflated figures has demonstrated that Soviet economic growth was never of world-historical magnitude. Witte, who in the 1890s achieved 8 percent annual growth in industry with far milder market methods, probably did as well as Stalin. And Meiji Japan, with 6 percent annual growth for its entire economy, did better, not to mention postwar Japan’s world record of 16 percent to 18 percent for its economy as a whole—or even Deng Xiaoping’s China at 10 percent to 12 percent in the 1980s.

zh: 但增长率远非衡量经济成功的唯一标准；斯大林工业化的代价也必须考虑在内。如果像他声称的那样，人是最宝贵的资本，那么集体化的六百万到一千一百万受害者就代表了对国家资源的巨大浪费。至于不那么宝贵的资本，还必须加上集体化造成的牲畜损失。而且，这项“投资”的结果并不是生产率更高的农业；相反，它创造了一个长期功能失调的农业经济。1939年，农村生活水平远低于1929年，实际上低于1913年；大多数城市人口的生活也只是略好一点。
en: But growth rates are hardly the only measure of economic success; the cost of Stalin’s industrialization must also be taken into account. If, as he claimed, people are the most precious capital of all, then the six million to eleven million victims of collectivization represent an exorbitant waste of national resources. As regards less precious capital, one must add the livestock losses of collectivization. The result of this “investment,” moreover, was not a more productive agriculture; it was, rather, the creation of a chronically disfunctional agrarian economy. In 1939 the rural standard of living was far below that of 1929, indeed, below that of 1913; and most of the urban population lived only marginally better.

zh: 直到斯大林死后，情况才有所改善；赫鲁晓夫和勃列日涅夫试图让集体农庄制度回到其最初目标，即提高农业劳动生产率。但即便那时，尽管向农村投入了巨额新投资，情况也从未显著改善。从结构上说，集体农庄毫无希望，因为集体劳动不给人任何生产激励。于是，1914年前曾是主要粮食出口国的俄国，在1970年代和1980年代经常不得不进口粮食（而印度和中国都能出口粮食）。这个制度的人的代价也继续高昂。俄国农民已经变成并将继续是一支士气低落、无精打采、很大程度上酗酒的劳动力，怀疑国家权力，不愿主动做任何事。
en: Nor would conditions improve until after Stalin’s death, when Khrushchev and Brezhnev sought to return the kolkhoz system to its original aim of increasing agricultural productivity. But even then conditions never improved significantly, despite enormous new investment in the countryside. Structurally, the kolkhoz was hopeless because collective labor gave no one an incentive to produce. Thus Russia, which before 1914 had been a major grain-exporting country, was regularly obliged to import food in the 1970s and 1980s (whereas both India and China were able to export it). And the human cost of the system continued to be high. The Russian peasantry had become, and would remain, a demoralized, listless, and largely alcoholic work force suspicious of state power and unwilling to take any initiative on its own.

zh: 这个一度被视为俄国最典型阶级的沦落，成为俄国文学的中心主题，从肖洛霍夫1932年的《被开垦的处女地》，到索尔仁尼琴1963年的《马特廖娜的家》，再到1970年代“乡村作家”的作品。这些作者隐含的信息是：集体化除了具有头等经济蠢行的性质之外，还是一种同等量级的罪行，不可磨灭地玷污了整个建立在农民白骨之上的制度。
en: The degradation of what had once been seen as Russia’s quintessential class would become a central theme of Russian literature, from Sholokhov’s
in 1932, to Solzhenitsyn’s

in 1963, to the works of the “Village Writers” in the 1970s. The implied message of these authors was that collectivization, over and above its character as an economic blunder of the first order, was a crime of the same magnitude, one that indelibly tainted a whole system built on peasant bones.

zh: 苏维埃工业化的资本确实如普列奥布拉任斯基所预见的那样，是从农民身上“抽”出来的。但这种融资方法由于其过度意识形态化的前提，事实上证明是一种无效的现代化公式。把苏联方法看作类似于近代早期英格兰通过剥夺农民进行资本原始积累，是不正确的，因为那里的资本并不是这样积累起来的。

今天没有严肃的经济史学家会主张，资本主义是建立在像剥夺农民土地这样简单的事情上，或者它的劳动力主要来自因此失去土地的农民。而且除英格兰的情况外，从未有人真正论证资本是以这种方式积累的。西方资本形成的来源实际上是多样而复杂的。但马克思主义需要一个整洁而有力的剥削历史逻辑，它在圈地剥夺的机制中找到了这个逻辑。通过剥夺庄稼汉来为社会主义工业化融资，同样需要一个简单而能推动行动的逻辑。于是，那场从未在英格兰发生的资本原始积累，实际上在斯大林治下的俄国以空前的残酷方式进行了。结果是集体农庄这个不育的制度，此后将始终是增长的障碍而非刺激。
en: The capital for Soviet, industrialization hud indeed been “pumped over” from the peasantry, as Preobrazhenskii had foreseen. But this method of financing in fact turned out to be an ineffective formula for modernization because of its excessively ideological premises. It is incorrect to view the Soviet method as analogous to the primitive accumulation of capital through dispossession of the peasantry in early modern England, for that was not how capital had been accumulated there.

No serious economic historian would argue today that capitalism was founded on anything so simple as the expropriation of peasant land, or that it drew its labor force primarily from a peasantry thus made landless. And aside from the English case, it has never really been argued that capital was accumulated in this manner. The sources of capital formation in the West were in fact varied and complex. But Marxism required a neat and compelling historical logic of exploitation, and it found it in the mechanism of expropriation through enclosure. The financing of socialist industrialization through expropriation of the muzhik also needed a simple, driving logic. Thus the primitive accumulation of capital that never occurred in England was actually carried out in an unprecedentedly brutal manner in Russia under Stalin. The result was the sterile institution of the kolkhoz that would remain ever after an impediment rather than a stimulus to growth.

zh: 诚然，在任何发达国家，传统农民都不得不让位于城市化力量。概略地说，这一过程始于农民迁往城市并成为工人；第二阶段，农村实现机械化，农民转变为农场主。这导致城乡差别逐步缩小（大体如马克思主义公式所主张的那样），最终结果是城市的压倒性优势，而先进国家的农村人口降到5%或更低。因此，传统农民最终在各地逐渐消失。
en: To be sure, in any developed country the traditional peasantry has to give way to the forces of urbanization. Schematically, this process begins with the peasants migrating to the cities and becoming workers; in a second phase the countryside is mechanized and the peasants are transformed into farmers. This leads to a progressive diminution of the differences between town and country (more or less as the Marxist formula holds), with the end result being the overwhelming preponderance of the city as the rural populations of advanced countries drop to 5 percent or lower. Thus the peasant winds up being phased out everywhere.

zh: 然而，真正的问题是达到这一结果的方式。在“资本主义”下，这用了几十年时间，主要靠市场压力（尽管欧洲共同体在1960年代和1970年代也通过曼斯霍尔特计划有意识地推动它）。其结果是，不到5%的人口就能为本国人提供极其充裕的食物，同时还出口大量粮食。在苏维埃俄国，农民的迁移用了十年（正如斯大林所说应当如此），并且是通过破坏性的国家行动实现的。但在那里，结果是农业组织的常年灾难，以及民族心灵上的一道持久创伤。因此，“现代化”很难说是对斯大林所造成之事的恰当称呼：我们面对的其实是意识形态统治和党治革命的极致。短期而言，这场革命允许基础工业化出现一次大冲刺，但长期而言，它留下了一个结构上残废的社会和经济。
en: The real question, however, is the way this is achieved. Under “capitalism” this occurred over decades and largely through the pressure of the market (though the European Community also consciously promoted it with the Meinhold Plan in the 1960s and 1970s). The outcome was a situation in which something less than 5 percent of the population was able to feed the home population almost sinfully well while also exporting great quantities of foodstuffs. In Soviet Russia the displacement of the peasant occurred over a decade (as Stalin said it should) and through destructive state action. But there the results were a perennially disastrous organization of agriculture and an enduring wound to the national psyche. Hence “modernization” is hardly an appropriate term for what Stalin wrought: We are dealing rather with the ultimate in ideocratic and partocratic revolution. In the short term this revolution permitted a great spurt of basic industrialization, yet for the long term it left behind a structurally crippled society and economy.

zh: 有人论证说，这一切之所以发生，只是因为斯大林走得太快。如果他能坚持计划最初的目标——五年内实现15%集体化——那么按照这种推理，农民本会被逐步争取过来，社会化农业本会证明比旧的孤立农户更具生产力。除了先验的信仰，没有理由相信事情会如此。长期经验表明，大规模机械化农业只对某些作物、在某些气候和地理条件下才优越；它并不是计划所设想的那种普遍有效的公式。
en: It has been argued that this occurred only because Stalin went too fast. If he had adhered to the Plan’s original goal of 15 percent collectivization in five years—so this reasoning goes—the peasants would have been won over gradually, and socialized agriculture would have proved more productive than the old isolated peasant households. There is no reason other than a priori faith to believe that this is so. Long experience indicates that large-scale mechanized agriculture is superior only for certain crops and under certain climatic and geographic conditions; it is not the universally valid formula that the Plan assumed it was.

zh: 同样，把集体农庄奉为一种更优越社会形式的崇拜，并非源于经济考虑，而是源于意识形态考虑。更准确地说，它源于把社会主义对集体劳动在道德上优于个体劳动这一观念的信奉，与对美国大草原大型机械化农场的理想化形象混融在一起（布尔什维克没有注意到，这种农场通常是家庭农场）。正因为如此，苏联所有制度中最不成功的一个，却成了官方苏联神话中最受珍视的一个。集体农庄被颂扬为社会主义劳动的顶峰——与真正的工厂相比，它确实是一种更集体的企业——并被宣布为苏维埃秩序的基石。斯大林以一座巨大的农业展览馆的形式，为这一制度建起神庙；几十年来，这座展览馆被当作所有访问莫斯科的人必须赞叹的对象。经过如此封圣，集体农庄简直无法放弃，即便面对越来越多证明其低效的证据，因为放弃它就等于否定整个制度。
en: Likewise, the cult of the collective farm as a superior social form derives not from economic considerations but from ideological ones. More precisely, it derives from a conflation of the socialist commitment to the moral superiority of collective over individual labor with an idealized image of the large-scale, mechanized American prairie farm (which the Bolsheviks failed to note was usually a family farm). It is for this reason that the least successful of all Soviet institutions became the most cherished in official Soviet mythology. Extolled as the acme of socialist labor—and compared to a real factory, it was indeed a more collective enterprise—the kolkhoz was proclaimed the bedrock of the Soviet order. Stalin erected a temple to this institution in the form of a giant Agricultural Exposition that for decades was presented as an object of mandatory admiration to all who visited Moscow. Thus canonized, the kolkhoz simply could not be given up, even in the face of mounting evidence of its inefficiency, because to do so would be to repudiate the whole system.

zh: 集体农庄（以及国营农场）之所以失败，并不是因为它推行得太快、强制性太强。相反，失败的根源在于这一制度的目的：把俄国的农民农场改造成农业工厂。就其本质而言，集体农庄是把城市—工业的马克思主义视角投射到农民世界上。此外，苏联马克思主义者由于敌视农民的落后，从来不想理解农村世界；他们只对改变它感兴趣。而这种极端的无知也大大促成了1930—1933年的灾难。
en: The kolkhoz (as well as the sovkhoz) did not fail because it was introduced too rapidly and through coercion. Rather, the cause of the failure lies in the institution’s purpose, which was to transform Russia’s peasant farms into agrarian factories. By its very nature the kolkhoz was a projection of the urban-industrial Marxist perspective onto the peasant world. Moreover, Soviet Marxists, because of their hostility to peasant backwardness, never wanted to understand the rural world; they were only interested in changing it. And this abysmal ignorance also contributed mightily to the catastrophe of 1930-1933.

zh: 然而当时也有人试图警告集体化的危险。例如，社会革命党经济学家亚历山大·恰亚诺夫论证说，农民天然的生产单位不是某种庞大的
，而是家庭，即由两三代人组成的扩大家庭。家庭自留地在整个苏联历史上的高生产率证明了这一点。恰亚诺夫还论证说，农民天然的联合形式是古典的生产者合作社；农民自己控制这种合作社，每个家庭在其中保持自己的经济身份。的确，革命前，农民俄国在社会革命党知识分子的帮助下，创建了欧洲最大的合作社运动之一。
en: Yet there were those at the time who tried to warn of the dangers of collectivization. For example, the SR economist Andrei Chaianov argued that the natural productive unit for the peasant was not some vast

but the household, which grouped two or three generations of an extended family. The high productivity of the individual family plot throughout Soviet history bears this out. Chaianov also argued that the natural form of association for the peasants was the classical producers’ cooperative, which the peasants controlled themselves and in which each household preserved its economic identity. Indeed, before the Revolution peasant Russia, with the aid of the SR intelligentsia, had created one of the largest cooperative movements in Europe.
